s: Start here - what this guide covers and where to find each topic.
x: Protequ User Guide Protequ is a web application for managing physical access: who may go where, with which credential, and what happened. This guide is for the people who use the application day to day. It tells you what to do and where to click. Each page covers one task or one idea, so you can look up an answer directly. Sections Basics slug:basics signing in, finding your way around, searching and working with lists. Concepts slug:concepts short definitions of the things Protequ manages: people, teams, credentials, devices, spaces and more. People slug:people the people and vehicles in the system. Teams slug:teams grouping people into teams. Credentials slug:credentials cards, PINs, license plates, biometrics and card decks. Devices slug:devices readers, controllers and other equipment. Spaces slug:spaces buildings, rooms and areas, and who is inside them. CCTV slug:cctv live view and playback of cameras. Authorization slug:authorization who may enter where and when. Audit slug:audit finding out who did or passed what, and when. Incidents slug:incidents handling alarms and security incidents. Scenarios slug:scenarios automated reactions to events. Card formats slug:card formats how card numbers are read. Licensing slug:licensing your licence and what it enables. Maintenance slug:maintenance settings and backup. Profiles slug:profiles profile templates. Some areas appear in your menu only if your licence includes them and your account may use them.

s: Find who did or passed what and when, in the event history of a person, team, device, space or the whole system.
x: Audit The audit is the record of everything that happened in the system: doors opened, access granted or denied, devices connecting and disconnecting, alarms, and changes made by operators. Every entry has a time, a severity and a sentence that names the people and devices involved. There is no single "Audit" entry in the main menu. Instead, the same audit list is built into the pages of the things you look after, so it already shows the events of that one thing. I want to... s: The Audit tabs of people, teams, devices, spaces, decks and incidents, and the recent activity on Home.
x: Where to find the audit Look for the Audit tab at the top of an item's page. It shows the events of that item only. Item Where A person Open the person, then the Audit tab. A team Open the team, then the Audit tab. A device Open the device settings and use the Audit tab. In the device navigator, an audit panel is docked at the bottom of the page, in Live mode. Drag its top edge to make it taller or shorter. It includes the events of the devices below the one you selected. A space Open the space, then the Audit tab. It includes the events of everything inside the space. A deck Open the deck, then the Audit tab. An incident Open the incident, then the Audit tab. See Incident audit slug:incident audit . Everything Home shows Recent Activity in Live mode below the system overview. A page scoped to one item shows only the events that mention that item and, for devices and spaces, the items inside it . The Home page is not scoped and shows events from the whole system. Related pages: People slug:people , Devices slug:devices , Spaces slug:spaces , Reading the audit list slug:audit reading events .

s: What each part of an audit row means and what the toolbar above the list does.
x: Reading the audit list The newest events are at the top. Each row has: a severity icon . The colour and icon grow more serious from Info through Warning, Error and Alarm to Fire Alarm and Critical. the time of the event, in your local time. a sentence describing what happened. Names of people, devices and spaces in the sentence are shown in bold. an image icon , on some rows, for example when a camera or reader captured a picture. Hover over it to see the picture. a three dot button at the right end of the row. See Create a scenario from an event slug:audit create scenario . When there is nothing to show, the list reads No events . The toolbar Control What it does Live / History Switch between watching new events and looking at a past period. See Live and History slug:audit live and history . Filters Open the filter window. A number badge shows how many filters are active. See Filter the audit slug:audit filters . Period menu History only Choose the time period. See Choose the time period slug:audit time range . Pause and bin icons Live only Pause the list and clear it. Expand icon Open the audit in a new tab. See Open the audit in a new tab slug:audit open in new tab . A list shows at most 1000 events. Narrow the period or add a filter if you cannot find the event you want.

s: Watch new events as they arrive in Live mode, or look at a chosen past period in History mode.
x: Live and History Every audit list has two modes. Switch with the Live and History buttons at the left of the toolbar. History History shows events from a chosen period, newest first. The default period is Last hour . Use it to answer "what happened yesterday evening at the main door". Change the period as described in Choose the time period slug:audit time range . Live Live shows events as they happen, newest on top. When you open it, it first loads the most recent events so the list is not empty. It keeps up to 1000 events. Click the pause icon to stop the list from moving while you read. Events that arrive meanwhile are held back. Click play to resume. Click the bin icon to clear the list and start fresh. Which mode opens first Lists in the item pages person, team, device, space open in History . Recent Activity on Home and the audit docked in the device navigator open in Live . The application remembers the mode you pick for each kind of list in your browser, so the next time it opens in the mode you last used. Related pages: Reading the audit list slug:audit reading events , Filter the audit slug:audit filters .

s: Pick a quick or relative period, or a custom date and time range, in History mode.
x: Choose the time period The period menu is shown in History mode. It is the button with the calendar icon that shows the current period, for example "Last hour". 1. Switch to History . 2. Click the period button. 3. Pick a preset: Preset Period Last hour, Last 4 hours, Last 12 hours, Last 24 hours counted back from now Today from midnight to now Yesterday the whole previous day This week from Monday to now Last week the previous Monday to Sunday This month from the 1st to now Last month the whole previous month A custom range 1. In the period menu choose Custom range... . 2. Pick the first and last day on the calendar. 3. Set Start time and End time . They default to 00:00 and 23:59:59. 4. Click Apply . Cancel closes the window. The period button then shows the range you picked. Related pages: Live and History slug:audit live and history , Filter the audit slug:audit filters .

s: Show only events of chosen severities, people, devices, spaces, teams or event types.
x: Filter the audit 1. Click Filters on the toolbar. The Filters window opens. A number badge on the button shows how many filters are active. 2. Under Severity , tick the levels you want: Info, Warn, Error, Alarm, FireAlarm, Critical. With none ticked, all levels are shown. 3. Use the Search... box to narrow the long list below it. 4. Use the chips All , Devices , People , Teams , Spaces and Event types to choose what kind of thing the list shows. 5. In the list under Entity / Type , tick the people, devices, teams, spaces or event types you want. The list updates the audit behind the window as you tick. 6. Click Close . Clear removes all filters. Several ticks of the same kind add up any of the ticked people . Ticks of different kinds narrow each other the ticked severities and the ticked devices . The Event types list contains every kind of event the system knows, for example "Access granted" and "Access denied", even when none happened in the current period. Filters stay while you switch between Live and History. They apply to the loaded list, so combine them with a suitable period slug:audit time range .

s: Use the audit of a door or space to see who was granted or denied access and when.
x: Find who passed a door 1. Open Devices and select the door or its reader in the device navigator, or open the Audit tab in the device settings. To look at a whole room, open the space and its Audit tab instead. 2. Switch to History and choose the period, for example Yesterday . See Choose the time period slug:audit time range . 3. Click Filters , choose the chip Event types , search for "Access" and tick Access granted people who got in and, if you also want refusals, Access denied . Close the window. 4. Read the list. Each row names the person, the door, the credential used, the direction when known, and the time. To see only one person at that door, also tick the person under the People chip. If a row says "unknown person", the card or code was presented but is not assigned to anyone. Related pages: Find what a person did slug:audit find person activity , Filter the audit slug:audit filters , Devices slug:devices .

s: Use the audit of a person to see every door they passed or were refused at.
x: Find what a person did 1. Open People and open the person. See People slug:people . 2. Open the Audit tab. 3. Switch to History and choose a period, for example This week . See Choose the time period slug:audit time range . 4. Read the list. It contains the events that mention the person, for example doors they passed and refusals. 5. To narrow it, use Filters . For example tick the severities Warn and above to see only problems. See Filter the audit slug:audit filters . If the person has several cards or other credentials, the events of all of them appear here. For a team, open the team and its Audit tab in the same way. Related pages: Find who passed a door slug:audit find who passed door , Where to find the audit slug:audit where to look .

t: Open the audit in a new tab
s: Open the current audit, with its filters, as a full page in a new browser tab.
x: Open the audit in a new tab 1. In any audit list, click the expand icon at the right end of the toolbar tooltip Open in new tab . 2. A new browser tab opens with the same audit as a full page view, titled "Audit". The new tab starts with the same scope, mode Live or History , severity filters, selected people, devices and event types as the list you came from. The page header shows the name of the source in the toolbar. Use this to keep an audit open on a second screen while you work, or to compare two periods side by side. This page is only reached from this icon. It has no entry in the main menu, and the icon is not shown inside the full page view itself. Related pages: Reading the audit list slug:audit reading events .

t: Create a scenario from an event
s: Right-click an audit row to start a new scenario based on that event.
x: Create a scenario from an event When an event is one you want the system to react to every time, you can start a scenario straight from the audit. 1. In an audit list, right click the event row, or click the three dot button at the right end of the row. 2. Choose Create scenario . 3. The scenario editor opens with a new scenario prepared from that event. Continue as described in The scenario editor slug:scenario editor . If the message "This event is still being saved try again in a moment." appears, the event is very fresh and has not been stored yet. Wait a moment and repeat. If "Could not create the scenario from this event." appears, try again later. This menu is shown in the main application only. Related pages: Scenarios slug:scenarios , Create a scenario slug:create scenario .

s: The list of access policies, what a Grant or Deny policy contains and what you can do from the list.
x: Access Policies Open Access Policies in the main menu to see every access policy. An access policy says that certain subjects people or teams may, or may not, enter certain objects spaces or devices , optionally only at certain times. What a policy card shows Each policy is a card with: a Grant or Deny label. Grant gives access, Deny takes it away. an Inactive label if the policy is switched off. the policy name. Subjects , the people and teams the policy applies to. Resources , the spaces and devices the policy covers. Schedules , the days and times when the policy applies. If there are none, the card shows "No time restrictions active at all times ". What you can do Task How Create a policy Click Create Policy , or use the arrow next to it to pick Grant Access or Deny Access . See Create an access policy slug:create access policy . Edit a policy Click the pencil icon on the card. See Edit an access policy slug:edit access policy . Delete a policy Click the bin icon on the card. See Delete an access policy slug:delete access policy . Find a policy Type in the search box in the top bar. The list narrows to policies whose name, subject or object matches. Select several policies Tick the check boxes, or Select All . The menu then offers Toggle Active and Delete . Show more policies on screen Turn on Compact view to see one policy per line. After you change policies, the new rights reach the devices through access synchronization. See Authorization slug:authorization and People slug:people .

s: The rules that decide the result when several access policies apply to the same person and door.
x: How access is decided A person can be covered by several policies at once, for example one for their team and another for them personally. These rules decide the result: 1. Nothing granted means no access. A person only gets in if some Grant policy covers them. 2. The most specific policy comes first. A policy that names the person directly is more specific than a policy for the team the person belongs to, and the team policy is more specific than a policy for a larger group above it. A more specific policy overrides a less specific one. 3. Deny wins. If a Grant and a Deny policy are equally specific, the Deny wins. 4. Time matters. A policy with a schedule only applies in the days and hours of that schedule. Grants from several policies add up, so a person who has a policy for 08:00 17:00 and another for 11:00 13:00 can enter 08:00 17:00. Example. Team "Employees" is granted the whole building. Person "John" is denied the server room. John can enter the building but not the server room, because the Deny names him directly. Devices apply the rights they receive during access synchronization. Whether a device understands every part of a policy, for example the holiday time window, depends on the device. See Schedules in an access policy slug:access policy schedules . Related pages: Access Policies slug:access policies , Create an access policy slug:create access policy .

s: Create a Grant or Deny policy, name it and choose who it covers and where.
x: Create an access policy 1. Open Access Policies in the main menu. 2. Click Create Policy to make a Grant policy. To make a Deny policy, click the arrow next to the button and choose Deny Access . The arrow menu also has Grant Access . 3. In the Create New Policy window, type the Policy Name . The name is required. 4. Under Subjects Who , search for a person or team in Add Subject and pick it. Repeat for more. The chips All , Person and Team narrow the search. 5. Under Objects Where , search in Add Resource and pick a space or a device. The chips All , Space and Devices narrow the search. 6. Optional: pick a Profile . See Profiles slug:profiles . 7. Optional: add a schedule with Add Schedule . Without a schedule the policy is active at all times. See Schedules in an access policy slug:access policy schedules . 8. Click Create Policy . The new policy appears as a card in the list and is Active . Use the Active/Inactive switch at the top of the window if you want to create it switched off. Use the bin icon next to a subject or object to remove it before saving. Related pages: How access is decided slug:how access is decided , Edit an access policy slug:edit access policy .

s: Change the name, subjects, objects, profile or schedules of an existing access policy.
x: Edit an access policy 1. Open Access Policies . 2. Click the pencil icon on the policy card. The Edit Policy window opens with the current values. 3. Change what you need: the Policy Name , the Active/Inactive switch, the Subjects Who . Add with Add Subject , remove with the bin icon. the Objects Where . Add with Add Resource , remove with the bin icon. the Profile , the Schedules When . See Schedules in an access policy slug:access policy schedules . 4. Click Save Changes . Cancel closes the window without saving. The Grant or Deny type cannot be changed in the window. To switch the type, create a new policy of the other type and delete the old one. After saving, the rights reach devices on the next access synchronization. Related pages: Access Policies slug:access policies , Delete an access policy slug:delete access policy .

s: Limit an access policy to days and hours, and give holidays their own time window.
x: Schedules in an access policy A schedule limits a policy to certain days and hours. A policy without schedules is active at all times. Add a schedule 1. Open the policy for editing. See Edit an access policy slug:edit access policy . 2. Under Schedules When , click Add Schedule . A schedule named "Schedule 1" appears. By default it is set to Monday to Friday, 08:00 to 17:00. 3. Change the Schedule Name if you like. 4. Under Days , click the day chips Mo, Tu, We, Th, Fr, Sa, Su to switch days on or off. A filled chip is on. 5. Under Time Range , set From and To . 6. Click Save Changes . You can add several schedules to one policy, for example one for weekdays and one for Saturday. Use the bin icon on a schedule to remove it. Different hours on holidays To give holidays their own time window, switch on Holiday Override in the schedule. A Holiday Time Range appears with From and To . On days that are holidays, this window is used instead of the normal one. Holidays come from the holiday calendar. See Holiday Calendars slug:holiday calendars . Related pages: How access is decided slug:how access is decided , Create an access policy slug:create access policy .

t: Enable or disable an access policy
s: Switch a policy off to stop it applying, or back on, without deleting it.
x: Enable or disable an access policy A switched off policy keeps all its settings but does not give or take away access. It shows an Inactive label on its card. One policy 1. Open the policy for editing with the pencil icon. 2. Use the Active/Inactive switch at the top right of the window. 3. Click Save Changes . Several policies 1. In the list, tick the check boxes of the policies, or tick Select All . 2. Open the menu that shows the number of selected policies, for example "3 selected". 3. Choose Toggle Active . Each selected policy is flipped: active ones become inactive and inactive ones become active. Related pages: Access Policies slug:access policies , Delete an access policy slug:delete access policy .

s: Remove one or several access policies permanently.
x: Delete an access policy Deleting removes the policy for good. If you only want to stop it applying for a while, switch it off slug:enable disable access policy instead. One policy Click the bin icon on the policy card and confirm the deletion. Several policies 1. Tick the check boxes of the policies. 2. Open the menu that shows the number selected. 3. Choose Delete . 4. Check the list of Items to delete and confirm. The window warns that the action cannot be undone. After the deletion, the rights the policy gave are removed from devices on the next access synchronization. Related pages: Access Policies slug:access policies .

s: Policies that decide what operators may read, change, delete or run inside the application.
x: App Policies App Policies are not about doors. They decide what operators may do inside the application itself, for example who can read or change people, teams, spaces or devices. Open App Policies in the main menu. The page works like Access Policies slug:access policies : a list of cards with a Grant or Deny label, subjects and resources, the same search, selection and Compact view , and the same pencil and bin icons. What is different in the editor Permissions. Four chips, Read , Modify , Delete and Execute . A filled chip is on. They say which operations the policy covers. Resources. The filter chips are All , App , Devices , Teams , People , Spaces and Decks . You can give a policy over application screens, devices, teams, people, spaces and decks. There is no Profile and no Schedules section. Create an app policy 1. Open App Policies . 2. Click Create Policy , or use the arrow to pick Grant Access or Deny Access . 3. Enter the Policy Name . 4. Choose the Permissions . 5. Add Subjects Who and Objects Where . 6. Click Create Policy . Edit, switch off and delete work exactly as for access policies. See Edit an access policy slug:edit access policy , Enable or disable an access policy slug:enable disable access policy and Delete an access policy slug:delete access policy .

s: What a holiday calendar is, where to find it and what you can do with it.
x: Holiday Calendars A holiday calendar is a list of dates that count as holidays or non working days. Access policies and devices use it to know when the holiday time window applies. See Schedules in an access policy slug:access policy schedules . Open Maintenance & Settings in the main menu and choose the Holiday Calendars tab. Each calendar is a card with its name and the number of holidays it holds. The icon is highlighted for the default calendar. Task Page Make an empty calendar and add dates by hand Create a holiday calendar slug:create holiday calendar Load public holidays of a country Import public holidays slug:import holiday calendar Rename a calendar, add or remove dates Edit a holiday calendar slug:edit holiday calendar Choose which calendar devices use by default The default holiday calendar slug:default holiday calendar Remove a calendar Delete a holiday calendar slug:delete holiday calendar If there are no calendars yet, the page says "No holiday calendars" and invites you to create one. You do not need a calendar unless some policy or device uses holidays.

s: Create a named calendar and open it to add dates.
x: Create a holiday calendar 1. Open Maintenance & Settings and choose Holiday Calendars . 2. Click Add calendar . 3. In the New holiday calendar window, type a descriptive name and click Create . 4. The calendar settings page opens. Add the holiday dates as described in Edit a holiday calendar slug:edit holiday calendar . The first calendar you create becomes the default calendar automatically. See The default holiday calendar slug:default holiday calendar . To fill a calendar from public data instead, see Import public holidays slug:import holiday calendar .

s: Load the public holidays of a country and year into a new or existing holiday calendar.
x: Import public holidays Holidays can be loaded from the public OpenHolidays service instead of being typed in. The import is a one time copy. Afterwards the calendar is yours to edit, and it stays unchanged when the public source changes. Import into a new calendar 1. Open Maintenance & Settings and choose Holiday Calendars . 2. Click Import calendar . The Import holidays from OpenHolidays window opens. 3. Fill in: Country code , for example CZ, SK, DE or PL. Required. Year s . One or more years separated by a comma, for example 2025, 2026. Required. Language code , for example CS or EN. Optional. Subdivision code , for example CZ PR or DE BY, to include regional holidays. Optional. 4. Click Import . A calendar is created and named after the country and years, for example "CZ 2026". The settings page opens so you can check the dates. Import into an existing calendar 1. On the calendar card click the download icon Import , or open the calendar and click Import at the top right. 2. Enter the Year s and click Import . When you start from a calendar that already has a country, the country field is not asked again. Imported dates are added to the calendar. Dates you added earlier stay. You are responsible for keeping the calendar up to date, for example by importing next year in December.

s: Rename a calendar, add or remove holiday dates and set it as default.
x: Edit a holiday calendar 1. Open Maintenance & Settings , choose Holiday Calendars and click the card or its pencil icon Settings . The Calendar settings page opens. 2. Change the Name . The change is saved when you leave the field. 3. To add a holiday, click Add date and pick a day. You can also type the date in the field. The date is saved at once and appears in the list below, grouped by year. 4. To remove a holiday, click the x next to the date in the list. 5. The number next to Holidays shows how many dates the calendar holds. 6. If there is more than one calendar, a Default calendar check box appears. See The default holiday calendar slug:default holiday calendar . There is no Save button. Name, default flag and dates are stored as you change them. Only the date matters. A holiday has no name in the calendar. To add many dates quickly, use Import public holidays slug:import holiday calendar .

s: One calendar can be the default that devices use unless they have their own.
x: The default holiday calendar One holiday calendar can be marked as Default calendar . Devices and functions that have no holiday calendar of their own use it. Where a device offers a holiday calendar setting, you can pick the Default entry or choose a specific calendar. See Devices slug:devices . Set the default The first calendar you create or import becomes the default automatically. When there are two or more calendars, open the calendar you want and tick Default calendar on its settings page. The text under it reads "Used as default for all devices without custom settings". Making another calendar the default changes the calendar used everywhere that is set to Default . No default You do not have to have a default. If none is set, devices that use holidays receive an empty list of holidays. Related pages: Holiday Calendars slug:holiday calendars , Edit a holiday calendar slug:edit holiday calendar .

s: Delete a holiday calendar that nothing uses.
x: Delete a holiday calendar 1. Open Maintenance & Settings and choose Holiday Calendars . 2. Click the bin icon on the calendar card, or open the calendar and use Delete calendar in the Danger Zone at the bottom of the settings page. The calendar is removed permanently and the action cannot be undone. A calendar that is in use cannot be deleted If a device or function still uses the calendar, nothing happens when you click delete and the calendar stays. First switch those devices to another calendar or to Default , then delete. Related pages: Holiday Calendars slug:holiday calendars , The default holiday calendar slug:default holiday calendar .

s: A short description of what Protequ does and what you can manage in it.
x: What is Protequ Protequ is a unified platform for managing physical security infrastructure. From one interface you can connect access control devices, manage people and their credentials, define spaces, set who may go where, and review everything that happened. The Home page lists the main features as cards, each with an Explore button that opens the area. Below them, a System Overview shows counts of people, devices, cards and policies. What you can do depends on your account. Menu items you may not use are not shown. See Concepts slug:concepts for the vocabulary used throughout this guide.

s: How to sign in to Protequ and how to sign out.
x: Signing in and out Sign in 1. Open the Protequ address your administrator gave you in a web browser. 2. If you are not signed in, the application sends you to the sign in page. Enter your credentials there. 3. After signing in you land in the application with the navigation menu on the left. Sign out 1. Click your name or avatar at the right end of the top bar. The user panel opens. 2. Click Logout . A page confirms that you have been signed out. Click Sign In Again to sign in once more.

s: Use the search box to jump to any item or to filter the list on the current page.
x: Searching and filtering The search box sits in the top bar. Its hint reads Start typing to search or filter . It does two things. Find any item 1. Click the search box. If you have searched before, your recent selections appear. 2. Type part of a name, internal number, e mail, phone, card code or similar. Results appear after a short pause. 3. Each result shows an icon, its name and its type, plus the field that matched. Types include people, teams, devices, spaces, scenarios, incidents, policies, cards, decks and events. 4. Click a result to open it. Click the X in the box to clear it. Filter the current page Under Filter on this page the dropdown offers filters for the page you are on. Typing text adds a free text filter option showing your text in quotes. Click it to apply; the list shrinks to matching items and the dropdown closes. Clear the box with the X to show the full list again. Which filters exist depends on the page.

s: Selecting items, bulk actions, adding items and switching to compact view in list pages.
x: Working with lists Pages such as People, Teams and Devices show their items as cards in a list. Select items Tick an item to select it. A counter shows how many are selected . Use Select all to select every item. With a selection, the commands for selected items for example delete appear next to the counter. Add an item Click the add button at the top of the list for example Add New Person , Add New Team , Add Device . A dialog opens; see Common dialogs slug:common dialogs . Compact view Switch Compact view on to show smaller rows and fit more items on screen. Your choice is remembered per list in your browser. Empty lists When a list has no items, a message such as No People Found is shown.

s: How the create dialogs and the delete confirmation behave.
x: Common dialogs Create dialogs Adding an item opens a dialog with a title such as Create New Person . Required fields show an error if left empty. Many fields have a short help text below them. Confirm with the dialog's main button or leave with Cancel . Delete confirmation Deleting never happens immediately. A confirmation dialog titled Delete opens with: a warning: Are you sure you want to delete the selected items? This action cannot be undone. the list of Items to delete , Cancel to keep everything, and Delete to confirm. Some actions that remove a link rather than an item for example detaching a card reuse this dialog with their own wording; read it before confirming.

s: Change the application language; the application uses a dark theme.
x: Language and display Change the language 1. Open Maintenance & Settings in the left menu, then General . 2. Under Language choose one of: English, Čeština, العربية, Magyar. The page reloads and the whole application switches to the chosen language. The choice is stored in your browser. Not every text may be translated in every language yet. Theme The application uses a dark theme. There is no theme switch.

s: What card formats are and where to manage them.
x: Card Formats A card format describes how a card number is shown in Protequ and how it is sent to readers and door controllers. The same card can be written in different ways depending on the reader technology, and a format keeps those variants together under one key. Open Maintenance & Settings in the menu and choose the Card Formats tab. In this section: Browse and find formats slug:card formats list Create a card format slug:card format create Edit a card format slug:card format edit Set up how the card number is displayed slug:card format display Add and edit transformations slug:card format transformations Try values in the live preview slug:card format preview Identify an unknown reader slug:card format identify Delete a card format slug:card format delete Card formats are used when you add cards to people; see Credentials slug:credentials .

s: See the list of card formats and filter it.
x: Browse and find formats 1. Open Maintenance & Settings and select Card Formats . 2. Each format is a card showing its name , its key , and chips with the card technology, the width in bits for example 26 b , the number of transformations, and System for built in formats. 3. Type in the Filter field to narrow the list. 4. Click the name or the edit pencil icon to open the format. If nothing exists yet you see No card formats ; use Add Format to create the first one. Built in System formats cannot be edited or deleted, but you can add your own transformations to them. See Edit a card format slug:card format edit .

s: Add a new card format with a name, technology and bit width.
x: Create a card format 1. On the Card Formats tab click Add Format . 2. In the Create Card Format dialog fill in: Name : a description for people. It is not part of the key. Technology : the card technology, the first part of the key. Format : the format part of the key, for example csn26 . Use only lowercase letters, digits and underscores. Canonical bits : the fixed width of the card value in bits 1 to 256 . 3. The Key line under the fields shows the resulting key. 4. Click Create . The format opens so you can continue with display slug:card format display and transformations slug:card format transformations . The key cannot be changed afterwards. If creation fails, check the key and try again.

s: Change the name and bit width and save a format.
x: Edit a card format Open a format from the list. The page has these parts: Definition : the format key locked, with the note Key cannot be changed , how many decks use the format, the Name , and Canonical bits . Display : how the card number is shown. See Set up how the card number is displayed slug:card format display . Transformations : how the value is sent to devices. See Add and edit transformations slug:card format transformations . Live preview : see Try values in the live preview slug:card format preview . Change what you need and click Save . If Canonical bits is not set, the other parts are dimmed until you set it. For a built in System format a banner explains that the definition is read only. You can still add your own transformations.

t: Set up how the card number is displayed
s: Choose Hex, Decimal or Fields rendering for a card number.
x: Set up how the card number is displayed The Display part of a format decides how the card number appears in Protequ. It does not change what is sent to devices. 1. Open the format and find Display . 2. In Rendering choose Hex , Decimal or Fields . Without a custom display the value is shown as raw hex. 3. With Fields , a bit ruler appears most significant bit on the left . Click Add field and for each field set Name , Bits , and whether it is Hidden for example reserved or parity bits; hidden fields are skipped when the number is shown . 4. The line under the ruler shows Covered x of y bits . If the fields claim more bits than the canonical width, an error says how many bits to remove and the format cannot be saved. 5. Click Save .

s: Define how a card value is encoded for readers and devices.
x: Add and edit transformations A transformation is a named channel that turns the card value into the form a device expects. Each is a pipeline of steps. The format's own channel is always listed first and carries the value unchanged. Add a transformation 1. In the Transformations part click Add transformation . 2. Enter a Name and the Spec segment , the third part of the key for example w26 ; lowercase letters, digits and underscores . The resulting Key is shown. A segment already used in the format is rejected. 3. Click Create . The transformation opens in its editor. Edit the steps Click a transformation row to open its editor. Use Add step and pick an operation: Reverse all bits , Reverse byte order , Reverse bits per byte , Swap nibbles these lose nothing Keep low bits , Keep high bits , Strip leading bits , Strip trailing bits marked lossy ; you give the number of bits Add Wiegand parity you give the payload bits; two bits are added and Zero pad left you give the target width Use the arrows to reorder steps and the bin icon to remove one. A warning says how many bits a lossy pipeline discards. Click Save . To remove a whole transformation open it and click Delete transformation . Some transformations carry a lock icon; those belong to the built in system set.

t: Try values in the live preview
s: Check how a card value is displayed and encoded before saving.
x: Try values in the live preview The Live preview on the format page lets you test a card value without touching any card. 1. Type the card value as hex into Canonical value hex . If the display uses Fields , you can type each field's number instead and the hex is composed for you. 2. On the left, Display shows how the number appears in Protequ. 3. On the right, On the wire lists the value of the format's own channel and of every transformation, with its bit width. A lossy channel shows how many bits it dropped. The transformation editor has its own preview: enter a Test value hex and Bits and see the value after every step. If the display fields exceed the canonical width, the preview shows an error instead.

s: Find which format an unknown reader produces from one sample card.
x: Identify an unknown reader If a reader sends a value you cannot match to a format, use the identification assistant. 1. On the Card Formats tab click Identify reader . 2. Enter True value hex what the card really holds and its bits, and Reader value hex what the reader produced . 3. Optionally narrow Technology ; the default is All technologies . 4. Click Find matches . Matching formats are listed. If none matches you see No library format produces that value ; build a custom transformation instead see Add and edit transformations slug:card format transformations . 5. Click Close .

s: Remove a card format you created, and what it affects.
x: Delete a card format 1. Open the format. At the bottom, in the Danger Zone , click Delete Format and confirm. Deleting removes the format and all its channels. Cards in decks bound to it lose those projections, and readers set to those keys fall back to the raw value. The page shows how many decks use the format. Built in System formats have no delete button.

s: Watch live and recorded camera video on a wall of tiles and control the cameras.
x: CCTV CCTV shows live and recorded video from the cameras and recorders connected to Protequ. You arrange cameras on a wall of tiles, control PTZ cameras, take snapshots and play back recordings. The CCTV area needs a licence for the video module and at least one camera or recorder added under Devices slug:devices . I want to... Go to Open the wall, change the grid, work with tiles Camera wall slug:cctv wall Put a camera on a tile, live or from a recording Add a camera to the wall slug:cctv add camera Move a PTZ camera, use presets, switch quality, take a snapshot Live view controls slug:cctv live controls Play recorded video, jump in time, change speed Playback slug:cctv playback Watch one camera in a floating window or separate browser window Floating window and single camera view slug:cctv viewer

s: Choose a grid layout and arrange, enlarge, detach and remove camera tiles.
x: Camera wall Choose CCTV in the main menu. The page is a grid of tiles that fills the screen. Layout The button at the top left shows the current grid. Click it and pick 1×1 , 2×2 , 3×3 or 4×4 . The default is 2×2. Your layout and the cameras on the tiles are remembered for your user in this browser, so the wall comes back as you left it. Quality follows the layout: a 1×1 wall shows the full quality HD stream, denser grids use the lighter SD stream to save bandwidth. See Live view controls slug:cctv live controls . Tiles An empty tile shows a plus button Add camera . Click it to choose a camera, see Add a camera to the wall slug:cctv add camera . A tile with a camera shows the camera name at the top left and a LIVE badge or REC for a recording at the top right. Click a tile to select it. Double click it to enlarge: the wall switches to 1×1 with that camera. Point at a tile to see the toolbar at its top right: Open in window Detach to window : moves the camera into a floating window and frees the tile, see Floating window slug:cctv viewer . Change camera : pick another camera for this tile. Remove from wall : empties the tile. Scroll over the picture to zoom in. A chip with the zoom factor appears; click it Reset zoom to return to the full picture. The controls along the bottom of a tile depend on the camera and on live or playback mode, see Live view controls slug:cctv live controls and Playback slug:cctv playback .

t: Add a camera to the wall
s: Pick a camera in the Select Camera dialog and show it live or from a chosen time.
x: Add a camera to the wall 1. On the camera wall slug:cctv wall click the plus on an empty tile, or Change camera on a tile that is already in use. The dialog Select Camera opens. 2. Type in Search cameras... to narrow the list. The search matches the name, the category and the type. The list contains the cameras, recorders and recorder channels you have added under Devices slug:devices . 3. Click a camera. The Stream Mode choice appears: Live : current video. Playback : recorded video. Choose the Date and Time to start from. Playback begins about 10 seconds before the time you chose, so you see what led up to it. 4. Click Add . Cancel closes the dialog. The camera appears on the tile. If it cannot be started the tile stays empty. The controls that appear on the tile PTZ, snapshot, speed and so on depend on what the camera supports.

s: Mute, switch SD/HD, take a snapshot and move PTZ cameras with presets.
x: Live view controls Point at a live tile to show its bottom bar. What you see depends on the camera. All cameras Mute / Unmute : video starts muted. SD / HD : switches between the lighter stream and the full quality stream. It is offered only for cameras that have both. The wall picks a quality automatically from the layout; your choice on a tile overrides it. Snapshot : saves a still picture of the current video. Offered only for cameras that support it. PTZ cameras Cameras that can pan, tilt and zoom show extra controls: Arrow buttons: Pan left , Pan right , Tilt up , Tilt down . The camera moves while you hold the button and stops when you release it. Zoom in and Zoom out . Home : return to the default position. Numbered Preset buttons: click a number to go to that stored position cameras with presets only . Store preset : click it, then click a numbered slot Save to preset N to store the current position. The Pick slot... hint reminds you to choose a slot. For recordings the bottom bar changes, see Playback slug:cctv playback .

s: Play recorded video from a chosen time, skip by a minute, change speed and use the timeline.
x: Playback Start playback by choosing Playback in Add a camera to the wall slug:cctv add camera . The tile shows a REC badge instead of LIVE. Controls Point at the tile to show the playback bar: Play / Pause . Back 1 minute and Forward 1 minute . Playback speed : opens a list of speeds. Offered only when the recorder supports it. Mute / Unmute . Timeline A Playback timeline sits above the buttons. Drag its handle, or click it, to jump to a time; the time is shown while you drag. Coloured markers on the timeline show moments the camera or recorder flagged: Motion detected Person / object detected Quality degraded Camera blinded Point at a marker to see its description. Back to live Pick the camera again with Live in the Select Camera dialog.

s: Keep one camera in a floating window or pop it out into its own browser window.
x: Floating window and single camera view Floating window Open in window on a wall tile moves that camera into a small floating window and frees the tile. The window stays on top as you move through the application, so you can keep watching a camera while you work elsewhere. In the window header: Drag the header to move the window; drag its corner to resize it. Minimize collapses the window to its header; the same button restores it. Open in new window arrow icon pops the camera out into a separate browser window. Close stops the video and closes the window. The window shows LIVE , REC or CONNECTING next to the camera name, and has the same bottom controls as a wall tile, see Live view controls slug:cctv live controls . Single camera browser window The pop out window shows one camera full screen with no menus. It starts at full quality; SD / HD is still available. While it connects it shows "Connecting...". If the camera does not exist or cannot be reached, a message says "Device not found" or "Failed to connect".

s: Short definitions of the things Protequ manages and how they relate.
x: Concepts Each page defines one idea in a few lines and points to the section that explains how to work with it. Person slug:concept person Team slug:concept team Credential slug:concept credential Device slug:concept device Space slug:concept space Authorization slug:concept authorization Audit and events slug:concept audit and events Incidents slug:concept incidents Scenarios slug:concept scenarios In short: people members of teams hold credentials . Devices read credentials and sit in spaces . Authorization decides who may use which space or device and when. Everything that happens is recorded as events and can be reviewed in the audit . Important events can raise incidents , and scenarios react to events automatically.

s: What a person is in Protequ and how it differs from a vehicle.
x: Person A person is an individual who can be given credentials and access rights. A person has a name and optional details such as first name, title and internal number. When you create a person you choose a category : Person or Vehicle . A vehicle is handled like a person so that it can hold a license plate credential and be granted access. A person can belong to one or more teams slug:concept team , holds credentials slug:concept credential and has access rights described in authorization slug:concept authorization . How to work with people: People slug:people .

s: What a team is and why you group people into teams.
x: Team A team is a group of people. Teams are hierarchical: a team can have sub teams. Grant access to a team once instead of to each member; the members receive it. A team has settings, members, sub teams, an image and an audit view. How to work with teams: Teams slug:teams .

s: What a credential is and which kinds exist.
x: Credential A credential is something a person presents to prove who they are at a reader. Protequ supports these kinds: Card a physical card. Cards come from a card deck a managed set of cards . PIN a code typed on a keypad. License plate for vehicles. Biometric for example a face template. OAuth an identity provider based credential. A credential is attached to a person slug:concept person . Whether it opens a door depends on authorization slug:concept authorization . How to work with credentials: Credentials slug:credentials .

s: What a device is and how devices relate to spaces and adapters.
x: Device A device is a piece of physical security equipment known to Protequ: a card reader, a door controller, a biometric scanner, a camera or a recorder. Devices are connected through adapters and appear in a tree: a device can contain other devices for example a controller with its readers and doors . You can see a device's state, send it commands and review its audit. Devices can be assigned to spaces slug:concept space . How to work with devices: Devices slug:devices .

s: What a space is - a place such as a building, room or area.
x: Space A space is a physical place: a building, a floor, a room or an area. Spaces form a hierarchy, so a building can contain floors and rooms. You assign devices slug:concept device to a space and can see who is currently inside Space occupancy . In the Czech interface spaces appear as Sektory . How to work with spaces: Spaces slug:spaces .

s: How access rights are defined - access policies, application policies and holiday calendars.
x: Authorization Authorization decides what is allowed. Protequ has two kinds of policies: Access Policies who may pass through which doors or enter which spaces, and under which conditions such as time of day. App Policies Application Policies what an operator may see and do inside the Protequ application itself. Policies can be given to people and teams. Holiday Calendars under Maintenance & Settings define holidays that time based conditions can use. After you change access rights, run access synchronization so devices receive them. See Navigating the application slug:navigating the app . How to work with authorization: Authorization slug:authorization .

s: Everything that happens is recorded as an event; the audit view lets you review it.
x: Audit and events An event is a record that something happened: someone passed a door, a card was added to a person, a device changed state, an operator changed a setting. Events have a time, a severity and a type. The audit is where you review events. Many detail pages a person, team, device or space have an Audit tab showing only the events related to that item. You can filter events, refresh the list and open the audit in a new tab. How to work with audit: Audit slug:audit .

s: What an incident is and how it reaches an operator.
x: Incidents An incident is an important situation that needs an operator's attention, raised from events. Active incidents show a count in the top bar. Operators can Accept , Defer and Resolve incidents, see the related events and add notes. Incidents need the matching module in your licence. How to handle incidents: Incidents slug:incidents .

s: What a scenario is - an automatic reaction to events.
x: Scenarios A scenario is an automatic reaction: when certain events happen, Protequ does something defined in the scenario, for example raising an incident. You create scenarios in the Scenarios area and can also import them. How to work with scenarios: Scenarios slug:scenarios .

s: The ways a person can identify at a device, and where to manage them.
x: Credentials A credential is what a person uses to prove who they are: a card, a PIN, a license plate, a fingerprint or face, or a login account. Credentials belong to a person. Whether the person may open a given door is a separate question decided by access rights; see Authorization slug:authorization . Types Type Used for How to add Card Card or tag at a reader Add a card slug:credential card add PIN Code typed on a keypad Add a PIN slug:credential pin add License plate Vehicle recognition Add a license plate slug:credential plate add Fingerprint , Face Recognition Biometric reader Add a biometric slug:credential biometric add OAuth Sign in account Add an OAuth account slug:credential oauth add Credentials are managed on the Credentials tab of a person. Cards additionally live in card decks , which group cards and decide how card numbers are shown; see Card decks slug:card decks . Tasks See and enable or disable credentials slug:credential manage Register a card with a reader slug:card enrol Edit a card slug:credential card edit Remove a credential slug:credential remove Create and manage card decks slug:card decks How card numbers are interpreted by readers: Card formats slug:card formats

t: See and change the status of credentials
s: List a person's credentials and enable, disable or mark them lost.
x: See and change the status of credentials Open People , then the person, then the Credentials tab or click the Credentials button on the person's card . Each credential is a card showing an icon, its type, its value for example the card number, the license plate, the account and a status chip. The credentials of a person are listed together; if none exists you see No Credentials Found . Statuses Status Meaning Enabled Can be used. Disabled Temporarily switched off. Lost Reported lost. Damaged Reported damaged cards only, set in Edit a card slug:credential card edit . Change the status of several credentials 1. Tick the credentials or Select all . 2. Open the selected menu in the toolbar. 3. Choose enabled , disabled or lost . Disabling a credential is the safe way to stop it working without losing it. The change reaches the devices on the next synchronization; see Send access to the devices slug:person sync access . Filter Typing in the search box filters the credentials by their value. Add and remove Use Add Credential see Credentials slug:credentials and the buttons on each card see Remove a credential slug:credential remove .

t: Add a card to a person
s: Assign an existing card, create a new one, or enroll it with a reader.
x: Add a card to a person A card always lives in a deck ; adding a card to a person assigns a deck card to them. 1. Open the person, Credentials tab. 2. Click Add Credential and choose Card . The dialog shows the person at the top and offers three methods. If there is no deck yet, the dialog says No Card Decks Yet ; click Add Deck , create one see Create a deck slug:deck create and come back. Method 1: Assign Card Use this when the card already exists in a deck and nobody holds it. 1. Search by name or number. 2. Click the card in the list each shows a status dot, its number and its deck . 3. Click Assign Card . The list contains only cards that are not assigned. If it is empty you see No cards available for assignment . Method 2: Create New Card Use this when the card is new and you know its number. 1. Enter a Card Label a name you recognise . 2. Enter the number. Depending on the deck's format you get one number box per field for example facility code and card number , or a single Code Value box for a raw hex value. If a format needs a parity bit you are asked to enter hex. 3. Pick the Card Decks deck if you have several. The deck you used last is preselected. 4. Click Create Card . The card is created and assigned to the person. Method 3: Enroll Card Use this to read the card with a reader instead of typing its number; see Register a card with a reader slug:card enrol . Optional PIN Below the methods there is a PIN Code box. If you enter digits, they are stored as a PIN for this card. If something goes wrong Could not assign card. Check the card and try again. is shown if the system refuses the assignment, with a reason when one is available. An invalid value shows The value is invalid .

t: Register a card with a reader
s: Present a card to a reader so the system reads its number, then assign or create it.
x: Register a card with a reader Enrolment reads a card's number with a reader instead of typing it. It is available as the Enroll Card method in two places: when adding a card to a person slug:credential card add and when adding a card to a deck slug:deck card add . You need a reader that supports enrolment see Devices slug:devices . Only such readers are offered in the list. Steps 1. Choose Enroll Card . 2. In Select Reader Device pick the reader. The reader you used last is preselected. Until you pick one the dialog says Select a reader to enroll a card . 3. Click Enroll . The dialog shows Waiting for card... 4. Present the card to the reader within 60 seconds. 5. The dialog shows Card read select an action below. What you can do depends on the card: Result What you see Action New card A form prefilled from the scan: Card Label , deck, Code Value Click Create Card . It is created and assigned when you started from a person . Known card, nobody holds it The card with its number Click Assign Card . Known card held by someone else {name} already holds this card Click Assign Card to give it to this person instead. Known card already held by this person This person already holds this card Nothing to do. Known card already in this deck deck dialog This card is already in this deck. with an Open link Nothing to do. Known card in another deck deck dialog Card "x" already exists in another deck. Move it here? Click Move here . While waiting Click Cancel Enrollment to stop Enrollment cancelled. . Problems Enrollment timed out. Try again. no card was read within the time. Enrollment failed. Check the reader and try again. the reader could not be reached. Check that the device is online.

s: Rename a card, change its number or status, or set a PIN bound to the card.
x: Edit a card Where On a person: Credentials tab, click the card or its Edit Credential pencil button. In a deck: Cards tab of the deck, the same button on the card; see Cards in a deck slug:deck cards . The dialog Edit Card shows the deck name under its title. Fields Field Notes Card Name Required. Status Enabled , Disabled , Lost or Damaged . Number One box per field of the deck's format, or Code Value hex when the format cannot be entered in fields. Card Decks Read only; shows the deck. To move a card to another deck see Cards in a deck slug:deck cards . PIN Code Optional PIN bound to the card. Click Save . If the system rejects a value, the reason is shown above the buttons. Changing the number of a card in use changes it for the person who holds it. Use Disabled or Lost instead if you only want it to stop working.

s: Give a person a numeric PIN, typed or chosen from suggestions.
x: Add a PIN 1. Open the person, Credentials tab. 2. Click Add Credential and choose PIN . 3. In Create PIN enter the PIN hint: a 4 8 digit code or pick one of the Suggested PINs chips. Suggest PIN shows new suggestions. The suggestions are free PINs, so they do not clash with an existing one. 4. Click Create PIN . The PIN must be numeric. The messages PIN is required and PIN must contain only digits are shown for missing or non numeric input. If the system refuses the value for example because it is already in use , it shows Invalid and offers fresh suggestions. The PIN then appears as a PIN credential on the person's card list. To change a PIN, remove it and add a new one; see Remove a credential slug:credential remove .

s: Register a vehicle's license plate as a credential.
x: Add a license plate License plates identify a vehicle at a camera that reads plates. They are usually added to a person with category Vehicle see Create a person slug:person create , but they can be added to any person. 1. Open the person, Credentials tab. 2. Click Add Credential and choose License plate . 3. In Add license plate enter the License plate vehicle registration plate . 4. Click Add . The plate must not be empty License plate is required . If the system rejects it you see Invalid license plate . The plate then appears as a credential. To change it, remove it and add the correct one; see Remove a credential slug:credential remove .

s: Enroll a fingerprint or face with a reader and attach it to a person.
x: Add a fingerprint or face The biometric data is captured by a reader, not typed in. 1. Open the person, Credentials tab. 2. Click Add Credential and choose Fingerprint or Face Recognition . 3. For a fingerprint, pick the finger in Select Finger from Right Thumb to Left Pinky . 4. In Select Reader Device pick a reader that can enroll biometrics. The dialog says Ready to enroll. Click 'Enroll' to start the enrollment process. 5. Click Enroll and present the finger or face to the reader Enrollment in progress. Please present your biometric to the reader... . 6. When the reader has captured it, the dialog shows Biometric Detected and closes. The new credential appears with the finger name or the type and the value Biometric data . To stop waiting click Cancel Enrollment . Close leaves the dialog without adding anything if nothing was captured. If the reader cannot be reached you see Enrollment failed. Please try again. If no reader is offered, no device that supports biometric enrolment is online; see Devices slug:devices . A person can hold several fingerprints, one per finger. To replace one, remove it and enroll again; see Remove a credential slug:credential remove .

s: Link a sign-in account to a person.
x: Add an OAuth account An OAuth credential links a login account to the person, so the person can sign in to the application. 1. Open the person, Credentials tab. 2. Click Add Credential and choose OAuth . 3. In Add OAuth Account fill in: Field Notes Account Required. The identifier the person signs in with. Temporary Password Initial password. The person must change it at the first login. 4. Click Confirm . If the account is empty you see Account is required ; if it cannot be created, Failed to create OAuth credential . To remove the account link see Remove a credential slug:credential remove .

s: Detach a card from a person or delete a PIN, plate, biometric or account.
x: Remove a credential On the person's Credentials tab each credential card has a button at the bottom. Card: Detach The button Detach broken link icon only takes the card away from this person. The card is not deleted: it stays in its deck with its history, and can be assigned to someone else. 1. Click Detach . 2. In Detach card read the note and click Detach . PIN, license plate, biometric, OAuth: Delete The button Delete Credential trash icon removes the credential permanently. 1. Click Delete Credential . 2. Confirm in the dialog. To delete a card itself not just detach it delete it from its deck; see Cards in a deck slug:deck cards . If you only want a credential to stop working for a while, set its status to Disabled ; see See and change the status of credentials slug:credential manage . The removal reaches the devices on the next synchronization; see Send access to the devices slug:person sync access .

s: What a card deck is, how the deck list works and what you can do with decks.
x: Card decks A deck menu: Card Decks is a named group of cards, for example "Employees 2026" or "Visitor badges". Every card belongs to exactly one deck. A deck is tied to a card format , which decides how the card number is entered and shown; see Card formats slug:card formats . Open Card Decks in the main menu. Each deck is a card with its name and description and the buttons Edit Deck settings; tooltip wording assumed , Cards and Delete Deck . The toolbar has Select all , a Compact view switch and Add Deck . The search box finds decks by name or description, and also cards inside them by name, number or holder. A deck has these tabs: Tab See Deck Settings Edit a deck slug:deck edit Cards Cards in a deck slug:deck cards Audit Audit of a deck slug:deck audit Tasks: Create a deck slug:deck create , Delete a deck slug:deck delete .

s: Add a new card deck.
x: Create a deck 1. Open Card Decks in the main menu. 2. Click Add Deck . 3. In Create New Deck enter a Name required and an optional Description . 4. Click Create . Set the card format and image afterwards; see Edit a deck slug:deck edit . If you try to add a card while no deck exists, the dialog sends you here; see Add a card to a person slug:credential card add .

s: Change the name, description, card format and image of a deck.
x: Edit a deck Open Card Decks , click the deck, and stay on the Deck Settings tab. Field Notes Deck Name Required, unique. Description Short description. Card Format The format that decides how card numbers are entered and displayed in this deck. Formats are managed in Card formats slug:card formats . There is no Save button. Image Click Upload Image . Supported formats: JPG, PNG, SVG. Maximum size: 5 MB. Changing the format changes how the numbers of all cards in the deck are shown.

s: List, edit and delete the cards of a deck.
x: Cards in a deck Open the deck and select the Cards tab. Each card shows its holder photo, or a card icon , its name, its number as rendered by the deck's format or No code assigned and its status. Edit Credential pencil opens Edit a card slug:credential card edit . Delete Credential trash deletes the card after a confirmation. This removes the card itself, not only its assignment; to only take it from a person use Remove a credential slug:credential remove . Tick cards to select several; the selected menu appears. Add cards with Add Card ; see Add a card to a deck slug:deck card add . If the deck is empty you see No Cards Found . The search box filters cards by name, number or holder.

t: Add a card to a deck
s: Create a card, move one from another deck, or enroll one with a reader.
x: Add a card to a deck Use this to build up the stock of cards before they are given to people. To give a card to a person directly, see Add a card to a person slug:credential card add . 1. Open the deck, Cards tab, and click Add Card . 2. Choose a method. Create New Card Enter a Card Label and the number number boxes per format field, or Code Value in hex . Click Create Card . If a card with that number already exists: in another deck you are asked Card "x" already exists in another deck. Move it here? Click Move here . in this deck you see This card is already in this deck. and cannot create it again. Move Move existing cards from other decks into this one. 1. Search in the box and pick cards; they appear as chips click the cross to drop one . 2. Click Move here n . Enroll Card Read the card with a reader; see Register a card with a reader slug:card enrol . A new card is created from the scan, a card from another deck is moved here.

s: History of events that concern the cards of one deck.
x: Audit of a deck Open the deck and select the Audit tab. It opens in History mode; switch to Live to watch events as they arrive and narrow the list with Filters . How to read and filter audit lists is described in Audit slug:audit .

s: Permanently remove a deck.
x: Delete a deck Deleting a deck cannot be undone. All cards in this deck will be unassigned. From the list Click Delete Deck trash on the deck's card and confirm. From the deck's page 1. Open the deck, Deck Settings tab. 2. In the Danger Zone , section Delete Deck , click Delete Deck . 3. Confirm. You return to the list of decks. To keep the cards, first move them to another deck; see Add a card to a deck slug:deck card add .

s: Add, organise, monitor and configure the physical devices connected to Protequ.
x: Devices A device is any piece of equipment Protequ talks to: a controller, a reader, a door, a camera, an intrusion panel. Devices belong to a tree: a controller contains its readers and doors, a recorder contains its cameras. Each device is handled by an adapter , the component that connects Protequ to that kind of hardware. Open Devices in the main menu to work with them. I want to... Go to See all devices and their state Device list slug:device list Register a new device Add a device slug:add device Load a device tree from a file Import a device slug:import device Browse one device tree, send commands, copy and paste devices Device navigator slug:device navigator Rename a device, change its picture or properties, delete it Device settings slug:device settings Check how full a controller's memory is Device synchronization slug:device synchronization See which spaces a device belongs to Device spaces slug:device spaces See what happened on a device Device audit slug:device audit Related areas: Spaces slug:spaces group devices into places, CCTV slug:cctv shows camera video, Audit slug:audit searches the full event history.

s: Find, filter and select devices on the Devices page, and see their current state.
x: Device list Choose Devices in the main menu. The page shows one card per top level device for example a controller or a recorder . Child devices such as readers and doors are reached through the device navigator slug:device navigator . What a card shows The device picture or a default device icon with a small badge that reflects its state. The device name and a short description. State chips , for example Online, Offline, Syncing or Restart Required. The buttons on a card are: Device icon : open the device. Clicking the name or picture does the same. Bin icon Delete Device : delete the device. Commands keyboard key icon : a menu of the commands this device supports, such as Restart. The list depends on the adapter. Checkbox : select the card. If no device exists yet, the page shows "No Devices Found" with a hint to use Add Device . Find and filter Type in the search box at the top of the application to filter the list on this page Filter on this page . Choose a type to narrow the list to one discipline: CCTV , ACC access control , EZS intrusion or EPS fire . Only disciplines that exist among your devices are offered. All types clears the filter. Select and delete several devices 1. Tick the checkbox on each card, or tick Select All in the toolbar. 2. The toolbar now reads "N selected". Open it and choose Delete Device . 3. A confirmation dialog lists the items to delete. Confirm to delete them. This cannot be undone. Compact view Turn on Compact view in the toolbar for a one line row per device. With a very long list the switch is locked on, with the hint "Large list: compact view is on". Next Add a device slug:add device · Import a device slug:import device

s: Create a new device by choosing an adapter, naming it and filling in its connection properties.
x: Add a device Use this when you register new hardware by hand. To build a whole device tree from a file instead, see Import a device slug:import device . Steps 1. Open Devices and click Add Device . The dialog Create New Device opens. 2. Pick the kind of device. The adapters are shown as a carousel: use the arrows or the dots to move, and read the name and description in the middle. 3. Under Device Settings , enter a Name . The name is required and should be unique. 4. If the adapter offers more than one kind of top level device, choose it in the Type list. 5. Fill in the properties shown below the name for example the network address . Which fields appear depends on the adapter. 6. Click Create Device . Click Cancel to close without creating anything. After creation you land on the new device in the device navigator slug:device navigator . Create a device and load its tree from a file Some adapters can read a vendor configuration file and build the whole tree of readers, doors and other child devices from it. For those adapters a Load configuration file button appears under the carousel. 1. Click Load configuration file and choose the file. 2. Fill in the name and properties as usual and click Create Device . 3. The device is created first, then the file is read in the background. A message says "Configuration import started". Child devices appear once the adapter finishes, and a second message reports success or failure. If it fails, the adapter log gives the reason. To remove the chosen file before creating, close the information box that appears under the button. If something goes wrong The dialog will not close on Create Device until the required name is filled in. If the adapter is not connected, the import cannot start and you see an error message instead of a device tree.

s: Load a device tree from an exported Protequ file or from a vendor configuration file.
x: Import a device On the Devices page click Import Device . The dialog accepts two kinds of file. File What happens A .json file exported from Protequ see Device navigator slug:device navigator , Export Protequ reads it itself and shows a preview: the root device name, its type and the number of child devices. A vendor configuration file of any other type Only an adapter can read it. Choose the adapter in the Adapter list. Adapters that cannot import files are not offered. Steps 1. Click Choose file and select the file. Exported .json files can be up to 5 MB. 2. For a vendor file, pick the Adapter . If only one adapter can import files it is selected for you. 3. Choose whether to create a new device tree or update an existing one. For an update, pick the target device from the list. Only devices that match the file and adapter are offered. 4. Click Import Device . The button is disabled until the required choices are made. A vendor file is read by the adapter in the background. You see "Configuration import started", then "Configuration import completed" or "Configuration import failed" the adapter log explains why . If the dialog shows "No adapter can import a configuration file", none of the running adapters supports file import.

s: Explore one device tree as a graph, run commands, copy or move devices, restart the adapter and export the tree.
x: Device navigator Open a device from the device list slug:device list to see its tree as a graph. The device you opened is the root; its children readers, doors, cameras and so on hang beneath it. Move around Pan and zoom the graph with the mouse. The percentage at the top left shows the zoom level, and the fit screen button next to it resets the view. Right click a device to select it and open the context toolbar above it. Search for a device by name in the search box at the top of the application to jump to it. Context toolbar Right click a device to show these buttons. Some appear only when they apply. Button What it does Add Device plus Add a new child device under the selected one. The menu lists the kinds that can go there. Navigate Open another device in the tree as the new root. Device Settings pencil Open the settings panel. See Device settings slug:device settings . Cut , Copy , Paste Move or duplicate devices, see below. Delete Device bin Delete the selected device. Expand all, collapse all Open or fold every branch of the tree. Commands keyboard key icon Run a command on the selected device, for example Restart or Synchronize Access. The list depends on the device. Cut, copy and paste devices 1. Select a device or several , then click Copy or Cut . The root device cannot be cut. 2. Select the new parent device and click Paste . Paste stays disabled if the move is not allowed, for example when you select more than one target for a cut or choose a device inside the cut branch. Restart banner When a change needs the adapter to restart, an orange banner appears: "Configuration has been changed. Restart the adapter to apply changes." Click Restart in the banner to apply it. Toolbar at the top left Audit opens the event panel at the bottom, see Device audit slug:device audit . Export downloads the device tree as a file you can load again with Import a device slug:import device . Device states Chips next to a device show its state, such as Online , Offline , Connecting , Degraded , Syncing or Restart Required . While a command waits for confirmation the chip reads Command pending .

s: Rename a device, edit its properties, change its picture, download adapter logs or delete it.
x: Device settings In the device navigator slug:device navigator , right click a device and click the pencil Device Settings . On a wide screen the settings open in a panel on the right, on a narrow screen in a dialog. The panel has the tabs Settings , Synchronization only for devices that support access synchronization and Space Config , plus a tab for each kind of device reference the device has. The Settings tab Device Name : required, and it should be unique. Next to it a magnifier button highlights the device in the graph. Properties : the fields depend on the adapter for example a network address . Device Profile Picture : shows the current picture. Click Upload Image to replace it. Supported formats are JPG, PNG and SVG, up to 5 MB. A bin button on a custom picture removes it. Diagnostic logs : Download logs gives you a zip with the adapter's recent logs to send to support. The button is disabled for devices without an adapter. Delete a device In the red Danger Zone at the bottom, click Delete Device . A confirmation dialog appears. Deleting a device cannot be undone. Device references Some devices link to other devices, for example a reader that belongs to a door. Each such link has its own tab where you choose the linked devices. Other tabs Device synchronization slug:device synchronization Device spaces slug:device spaces

s: See how much of a controller's memory is used by the access data sent to it.
x: Device synchronization Protequ sends access data people, credentials, rights to controllers that keep their own copy. The Synchronization tab shows how full the controller's memory is. The tab appears in Device settings slug:device settings only for devices that support the commands Synchronize Access or Synchronize Antipassback . Memory occupancy The tab lists each memory segment of the device with "used / capacity" and a bar: green: under 80 % orange: 80 % or more red: 95 % or more A segment without a known capacity shows only the used count. Until the device has reported anything, the tab says "No synchronization data yet". The figures refresh when a synchronization run finishes. Run a synchronization To start a synchronization by hand, open the Commands menu in the device navigator slug:device navigator and choose Synchronize Access , Synchronize Antipassback or Full Access Synchronization . While it runs the device shows the state Syncing , and Sync Failed if it did not complete.

s: See which spaces a device is assigned to and set its direction in each of them.
x: Device spaces The Space Config tab in Device settings slug:device settings lists every space the device is assigned to, as a card per space with its name. Each card holds the device's settings for that space. When the space uses antipassback or occupancy limits, a reader can be given a Reader Role Entry or Exit , which tells Protequ the direction of passage. Without those features the role is not shown. See Space settings slug:space settings . If the device is in no space, the tab says "This device is not assigned to any space". To assign it, open the space and use Space devices slug:space devices .

s: Watch live events from a device tree and everything beneath it.
x: Device audit In the device navigator slug:device navigator , click the Audit icon in the top left toolbar. A panel opens at the bottom of the page. It shows events from the opened device and all its child devices, starting in live mode, so new events appear as they arrive. Drag the top edge of the panel to make it taller or shorter. Click a device name in an event to highlight that device in the graph. Click the icon again to close the panel. The panel works like the main audit view: you can filter, search and switch to history. See Audit slug:audit for details.

s: See, take over and close the incidents that need an operator, from the list, the alarm panel or the detail page.
x: Incidents An incident is something that needs an operator's attention, for example a forced door or a repeated access refusal. Incidents are created by scenarios slug:scenarios and arrive in a queue. An operator accepts an incident, follows its instructions and resolves it. Incidents need the matching licence module. If the Incidents entry is missing from the main menu, ask your administrator. This section is about the main application. The separate Monitor application has its own manual. I want to...
