Go to See all incidents of a period and filter them The incident list slug:incidents list Act on incidents from any page The incident panel slug:incident panel Take an incident over Accept an incident slug:incident accept Close an incident Resolve an incident slug:incident resolve Pause work on an incident and come back to it Defer and resume slug:incident defer resume Work through the steps an incident asks for Incident instructions slug:incident instructions Read everything about one incident Incident detail slug:incident detail Handle many incidents at once Accept and resolve several incidents slug:incident bulk See incidents that were hidden from the queue Suppressed incidents slug:incident suppressed See every event behind an incident Incident audit slug:incident audit Remove an incident record Delete an incident slug:incident delete See also the concept page Incidents slug:concept incidents .

s: The Incidents page lists incidents of a chosen period, with phase filter, counts and selection.
x: The incident list Open Incidents in the main menu. What you see Each incident is a card with: its title a summary of what happened , a phase label, Active , Resolved or Closed , its status , for example Pending , In Progress or Deferred , the number of events behind it and its Duration , how it ended for example Real Threat or False Alarm once it is resolved, a note count, when notes exist, and its age. Active incidents are listed first, ordered by priority and then newest first. Resolved and closed ones follow. When nothing matches, the page says No Active Incidents . Narrow the list Control What it does Period button Choose the period. The list opens on Today . The presets are the same as in the audit, see Choose the time period slug:audit time range . Refresh icon Reload the list. All / Active / Resolved Show only incidents of that phase. Search or filter in the top bar The filter box Filter Incidents keeps incidents whose severity, status, phase or event type contains your text. Totals on the right Total , Active and Resolved counts of the period. Open or select Click a card to open the incident detail slug:incident detail . Tick the check box on a card, or Select All , to select incidents. Resolve selected opens the one selected incident, or, when you selected several, starts a bulk resolve slug:incident bulk . Clear selection unticks everything.

s: The alarm icon, the floating button and the panel that lets you handle active incidents from any page.
x: The incident panel You do not have to open the Incidents page to react. When there is at least one active incident, an alarm button appears: in the top bar , with a red badge showing the number of active incidents, and as a round floating button at the bottom right of the page while the panel is closed. The icon and its glow reflect the highest severity among the visible incidents, from Info up to Critical. When a new incident arrives, the application plays an alert sound. Click either button to open the panel Active Alarms n . You can drag it by its header and close it with the x . A row in the panel Each row shows a severity dot, a summary, the status and the age of the incident. The buttons at the right depend on the status: Status Buttons Pending Accept In Progress you Real , False , Unknown to resolve, and Defer Deferred yours Resume any View , which opens the incident detail slug:incident detail An incident taken by another operator shows In Progress with the operator's name and has no action buttons for you. Click a row to expand it. The expanded row shows severity, status, owner and duration, the instruction steps slug:incident instructions or the timeline, and the notes. At the bottom of the panel, Accept All and Resolve all... start bulk work. See Accept and resolve several incidents slug:incident bulk . If no active or suppressed incidents remain, the panel closes by itself.

s: Take over a pending incident so that you own it and can work on it.
x: Accept an incident A new incident is Pending and belongs to nobody. Accepting it makes you the owner and moves it to In Progress you . 1. Open the incident panel slug:incident panel with the alarm button, or open the incident detail. 2. Click Accept the check circle icon on the pending incident. Now the instruction steps can be worked and the resolve buttons appear. If another operator accepted the incident a moment earlier, you see "Incident was accepted by another operator" and the incident shows their name. To accept all pending incidents at once, see Accept and resolve several incidents slug:incident bulk . Related pages: Resolve an incident slug:incident resolve , Defer and resume slug:incident defer resume .

s: Close an incident you own by classifying it as a real threat, a false alarm or unknown.
x: Resolve an incident The resolve buttons are offered on an incident that is In Progress . In the panel they appear only on your own incidents. 1. Open the incident panel slug:incident panel or the incident detail slug:incident detail . 2. Click one of the three result buttons: the check icon, Real , for a real threat, the cross icon, False , for a false alarm, the question mark icon, Unknown , when you cannot tell. The incident moves to the Resolved phase and shows the result, for example Real Threat , False Alarm or Unknown . When the buttons are grey If the incident has mandatory instruction steps that are not done yet, the three buttons are disabled and the page shows "Resolve blocked N mandatory step s awaiting confirmation". Finish those steps first. See Incident instructions slug:incident instructions . If the server still refuses the resolution because a mandatory step is open, the same message appears as a notice. No reason or note The buttons resolve at once. There is no field for a note or a false alarm cause on these buttons. Add notes through a Note step in the instructions. Several incidents can be resolved together, see Accept and resolve several incidents slug:incident bulk .

s: Put an incident of yours on hold and take it up again later.
x: Defer and resume If you cannot finish an incident right now, defer it instead of resolving it. Defer 1. On an incident that is In Progress you , click the pause icon, Defer . You find it in the incident panel slug:incident panel and in the top right of the incident detail slug:incident detail . 2. The status becomes Deferred . Resume 1. On the deferred incident, click the play icon, Resume . 2. The status returns to In Progress you and you can continue. A deferred incident stays yours and stays in the list. It is not closed. Related pages: Resolve an incident slug:incident resolve .

s: Work through the steps an incident asks for: confirm information, add notes and run actions.
x: Incident instructions Some incidents come with a checklist of Instructions . They were prepared by whoever wrote the scenario that created the incident. See Scenario instructions slug:scenario instructions . You find the steps in the incident detail slug:incident detail under Instructions , and in an expanded row of the incident panel slug:incident panel under Steps . A progress indicator shows how many steps are done and how many of the mandatory ones. Kinds of step Step What you see What you do Information Text. A check box only if the step is mandatory. Read it. Tick the box to confirm a mandatory one. Note A text box with "Quick note..." and a send button. Type your note and send it. It is added to the incident. Command A button named after the command, or Execute . Click to run the command on the device. The button then shows Executed . Show on map Show on map Click to jump to the place. Verify identity Verify identity Click to look at the person. Capture Capture Click to take a snapshot. Escalate Escalate Click to escalate to the named person. Notify Notify Click to send the prepared notification. A step marked Mandatory must be done before the incident can be resolved. See Resolve an incident slug:incident resolve . A step labelled "Unavailable no source target" cannot be run, because the event that raised the incident did not point to a device or place. Executed steps and notes appear in the incident's timeline.

s: The detail page of one incident: summary, instructions, timeline and its Audit tab.
x: Incident detail Open an incident by clicking its card in the incident list slug:incidents list , or View in the incident panel slug:incident panel . The page has two tabs at the top, Summary and Audit . Summary The Summary tab has these parts. Summary panel. The incident title with action buttons at its right, depending on the status: Pending , Accept . In Progress , the resolve buttons Real , False , Unknown , and Defer . Deferred , Resume . Below it, the fields Severity , Phase , Status and Owner shown when there is one , Created , Last Activity and Duration , and, once resolved, Resolution and False Alarm Cause . Instructions. Shown only when the incident carries steps. See Incident instructions slug:incident instructions . Timeline. Always shown. The history of the incident: when it was raised, the events, operator actions, executed steps and notes, with the operator's name and, where there is one, a picture. Danger Zone. At the bottom, Delete Incident . See Delete an incident slug:incident delete . If the incident cannot be loaded, the page says Incident Unavailable . Audit The Audit tab lists the events behind the incident. See Incident audit slug:incident audit .

s: Accept all pending incidents and resolve a group of incidents in one go, with merged steps.
x: Accept and resolve several incidents When many alarms arrive together, for example from one event that hits several doors, handle them as a group. Accept all In the incident panel slug:incident panel , click Accept All at the bottom. It shows only while some incident is Pending . All pending incidents become yours and a message tells how many were accepted, for example "Accepted 4 incidents". The panel then enters a bulk session. Start a bulk session You can also start one without accepting first: In the panel, click Resolve all... at the bottom, or On the incident list slug:incidents list , select two or more incidents and click Resolve selected . In a bulk session The incidents you can act on collapse into one row titled Bulk resolve , listing their names and Bulk N incidents . Under it: the steps of all incidents are merged. A step shared by several incidents appears once with a count such as "x3". Doing it once does it for each incident. A note typed in a note step is added to every incident of the group. a combined timeline of all the incidents. the progress of steps and mandatory steps. To finish, click the flag icon Resolve all... at the top of the row and choose Real , False or Unknown . All incidents in the group are resolved with that result and a message such as "Resolved 4 incidents" appears. If mandatory steps are still open, resolving is blocked with the message "Resolve blocked N mandatory step s awaiting confirmation". If none of the selected incidents can be resolved now, you see "None of the selected incidents can be resolved right now". Click Cancel bulk at the bottom to leave the bulk session without resolving. Work already done on steps is kept. Related pages: Resolve an incident slug:incident resolve , Incident instructions slug:incident instructions .

s: Show and restore incidents that were hidden from the active queue.
x: Suppressed incidents A suppressed incident is hidden from the active queue so that it does not distract operators, but it is not deleted. It does not count in the alarm badge and does not change the alarm button colour. Show them When some incidents are suppressed, the incident panel slug:incident panel shows a line Show N suppressed above the footer. Click it to list them. Click Hide suppressed to fold them again. Bring one back Click the Unsuppress icon on the suppressed incident. It returns to the active queue. Related pages: The incident list slug:incidents list .

s: The Audit tab of an incident lists the events of the people and devices involved, from the incident start.
x: Incident audit 1. Open the incident detail slug:incident detail . 2. Click the Audit tab at the top. The audit list is scoped to the people and devices the incident involves. It starts at the moment the incident was created. For an active incident the list stays open ended, so it follows what happens next. For a resolved one it ends at the incident's last activity. The list works as everywhere else in the application: filters, Live and History , and the period menu. See Reading the audit list slug:audit reading events and Filter the audit slug:audit filters . Click the Summary tab to go back to the incident.

s: Permanently remove an incident record from the detail page.
x: Delete an incident Deleting removes the incident record. Normally you resolve an incident instead, see Resolve an incident slug:incident resolve . 1. Open the incident detail slug:incident detail . 2. Scroll to the Danger Zone at the bottom. 3. Click Delete . The text above it reads "Once you delete this incident, there is no going back." 4. Check the incident in the Items to delete list and confirm. You return to the incident list slug:incidents list .

s: Check your licence, request a new one and import it.
x: Licensing Protequ needs a valid licence to run. A new installation starts with a trial period. Open Licensing in the main menu to see where you stand. In this section: Read the licence status slug:licensing status Request and import a licence slug:licensing import See what your licence includes slug:licensing entitlements Licence problems and what they mean slug:licensing problems

s: The Licence Status card: state, dates and warnings.
x: Read the licence status On the Licensing page the License Status card shows a coloured chip with the current state and a table: Customer License ID Valid From and Valid To Grace Until Trial Ends The main states are Valid , Grace Period the licence has run out but the system still works for a limited time , Trial and Expired . See Licence problems and what they mean slug:licensing problems for the rest. Any warnings appear in a yellow box under the table.

s: Download an activation request and import the licence you receive.
x: Request and import a licence 1. On the Licensing page, in the Activation Request card, click Download Request . A file is downloaded and a note says a new activation request has been generated. 2. Send that file to your Protequ contact. It identifies the installation only; the licensed capacities come in the licence you receive. 3. When the licence file .pqlic arrives, click Import License and choose it. It is imported straight after you pick it. 4. A message confirms the result and the status card refreshes. A failed import shows an error message.

s: Modules, adapters, device capacity and running allocations.
x: See what your licence includes Two cards on the Licensing page show what you may use. Entitlements Modules : the Protequ modules covered. Adapters : the adapters you may run. Device Capacities : for each Category , Usage as used/allowed . Running Allocations lists the adapters currently using capacity: Adapter , Root Device and Last Seen . With nothing running you see No active allocations . Some areas, such as CCTV or Maintenance modules, are available only when covered here.

t: Licence problems and what they mean
s: The error states shown in the licence chip and what to do.
x: Licence problems and what they mean The status chip can show a red problem state: State What to do Expired Request and import a new licence. See Request and import a licence slug:licensing import . Clock Rollback Detected The server clock went backwards. Correct the system time, then click Acknowledge Clock Rollback . Invalid Signature , Unsupported Schema , License State Corrupt , Trial Tampered The licence cannot be accepted. Contact Protequ support. Activation Request Missing or Mismatch , Fingerprint Mismatch The licence does not belong to this installation or request. Download a new request and ask for a matching licence. Unknown The status could not be read. Reload; if it persists contact support.

s: Settings and maintenance tabs: language, card formats, holiday calendars and backup.
x: Maintenance & Settings Maintenance & Settings in the main menu groups administration pages as tabs. Opening it takes you to the first tab. The tabs you can see depend on your installation: General : language slug:maintenance language Card Formats : see Card Formats slug:card formats Holiday Calendars : see Authorization slug:authorization DB Backup : back up and restore the database slug:maintenance backup The DB Backup tab appears only when the database backup module is installed and licensed.

s: Pick the display language of the application.
x: Change the language 1. Open Maintenance & Settings , tab General . 2. In Language choose English , Čeština , العربية or Magyar . 3. The page reloads and the whole application switches to the chosen language. The choice is remembered in your browser, so it applies on this browser only.

s: Run a database backup and read the backup list and activity log.
x: Back up the database Open Maintenance & Settings , tab DB Backup . Click Backup Now to create a backup. A progress bar shows while it runs, then Backup completed. appears. The table lists backups still available: Started , Status , Trigger , Size , Artifact file name and a Restore button. A backup made automatically before a restore shows Pre restore as the trigger. With none you see No local backups yet. Only the newest backups are kept, so older ones disappear from the list. Below the table an activity log shows backup and restore events with their history. To go back to a backup, see Restore the database slug:maintenance restore .

s: Overwrite the live database from a backup, with the safety steps.
x: Restore the database Restoring replaces all current data with the contents of a backup. Use it only when you are sure. 1. On the DB Backup tab find the backup in the table and click its Restore icon. 2. The DANGER ZONE — Restore database dialog names the backup file. It warns that the live database is overwritten, the server briefly disconnects, and the change is irreversible. 3. A safety backup is taken automatically first it appears later with trigger Pre restore . 4. Type restore now in the box. The Restore overwrite button stays disabled until you do. 5. Click Restore overwrite . When done you see Restore completed — the live database was overwritten. A failure shows Restore failed with the reason. Click Cancel to leave without changes.

s: What the People area contains and how its pages fit together.
x: People The People area holds everyone who can be given access: employees, visitors, contractors, and also vehicles. Open it from People in the main menu. A person has its own set of pages, shown as tabs once you open a person: Tab What it is for Settings Name, contact details, photo. See Edit a person slug:person edit . Teams The teams the person belongs to. See Teams of a person slug:person teams . Credentials Cards, PINs, license plates, biometrics. See Credentials slug:credentials . Access state What the person may open and whether it has reached the devices. See Access of a person slug:person access . Audit History of what happened to and with the person. See Audit of a person slug:person audit . Common tasks Find people in the list slug:people find Create a person slug:person create Edit a person slug:person edit Add a person to a team or remove them slug:person teams Check the access of a person slug:person access Send access to the devices slug:person sync access Delete a person slug:person delete A person can also be a Vehicle . Vehicles are used for license plate access; see Add a license plate slug:credential plate add . To grant or withdraw access rights see Authorization slug:authorization .

s: Search, filter by category, select several people and change the list density.
x: Find people in the list Open People in the main menu. Each person is shown as a card with the photo, the name, and the teams the person belongs to Member of teams: . Search and filter Use the search and filter box at the top of the app hint: Start typing to search or filter . Filter on this page narrows the list to people whose name contains what you typed. All , Person and Vehicle limit the list to one category. All removes the category limit. Open a person Click the photo or name to open the person's Settings . The buttons at the bottom of a card or on the right in compact view are shortcuts: Button tooltip Opens Edit Settings tab Teams Teams tab Credentials Credentials tab Delete Delete confirmation, see Delete a person slug:person delete Commands menu Synchronize Access , see Send access to the devices slug:person sync access The tooltip texts of the first four buttons may read slightly differently in your version. Select several people Tick the checkbox on each card, or tick Select all in the toolbar. The toolbar then shows how many people are selected ; open that menu to run a command for all of them Synchronize Access . Compact view The Compact view switch in the toolbar shows one narrow row per person instead of a card. On a very long list the app turns compact view on by itself and locks the switch Large list compact view is on . Empty list If you see No People Found , nobody has been added yet. Use Add New Person ; see Create a person slug:person create .

s: Add a new person or vehicle and fill in its basic details.
x: Create a person 1. Open People in the main menu. 2. Click Add New Person top right . 3. In the dialog Create New Person fill in the fields: Field Notes Surname Required. Shown as Surname is required if empty. Category Person or Vehicle . Cannot be changed later. First Name Only for category Person. Title Only for category Person job title or position . Internal Number Only for category Person employee or reference number . Email Only for category Person. Phone Only for category Person. For a Vehicle only the name field is shown. 4. Click Create Person . The new person opens on the Settings tab. Click Cancel or press Esc to close the dialog without creating anything. Next steps Add a photo and extra details: Edit a person slug:person edit . Give the person a way to identify: Credentials slug:credentials . Put the person into a team so access rights apply: Teams of a person slug:person teams . If you create the person from a team's Team Members page, the person is placed in that team straight away; see Team members slug:team members .

s: Change the name, contact details and photo of a person on the Settings tab.
x: Edit a person Open the person click it in the list and stay on the Settings tab. Details Field Notes Surname Required. The name cannot be left empty. Category Read only. Set when the person was created. First Name , Title , Internal Number , Email , Phone Only for category Person. There is no Save button. Additional detail fields defined for your installation, if any, appear below these fields. Profile picture 1. Click Upload Image on the right. 2. Choose a file. Supported formats: JPG, PNG, SVG. Maximum size: 5 MB. The picture is shown on the person's card in the list. Other tabs The tabs at the top lead to Teams , Credentials , Access state and Audit of the same person. See People slug:people . To remove the person see Delete a person slug:person delete .

s: See which teams a person belongs to, add the person to a team or remove them.
x: Teams of a person Open the person and select the Teams tab. It lists the teams the person is a member of. Teams matter because access rights given to a team apply to all its members; see Check the access of a person slug:person access . Add the person to an existing team 1. Click Add Existing Team . 2. Search for the team in the dialog, pick one or more they appear as chips , and confirm. Only teams the person is not yet in are offered. Create a new team for the person Click Add New Team , fill in the dialog see Create a team slug:team create and confirm. The new team is created and the person becomes its member. Remove the person from a team 1. Tick the team's checkbox or Select all . 2. Open the selected menu in the toolbar and choose Remove . 3. Confirm the dialog. The team and its other members are not changed. Use this menu rather than the trash button on a team card: that button may delete the whole team, not only the membership. If the person has no teams you see No Teams Found .

s: Read the Access state tab: which access rights a person has and whether the devices already know them.
x: Access of a person Open the person and select the Access state tab page title Access rights . It answers two questions for every door or other device the person is related to: Assigned does the person have the right in the system? Applied has that right reached the device? The list is grouped by space. Click the name of a space to open it. Click Refresh to reload. Some labels on this page are not yet translated in the app and may read differently. Assigned Icon Meaning Green check The person has access. Red block Access is denied. Applied Icon Meaning Cloud with check Fully applied; the time of the last synchronization is shown next to it. Cloud with arrows Partly applied. Red error There is a problem. Cloud off Not applied. Details of one entry Click a row. A panel opens on the right with: the result for the person Allowed or Blocked , the synchronization status and Last synchronized , Why access the policies behind the result. Each policy shows whether it grants or denies, where it comes from Direct person assignment or the name of the team that passed it on and its time restrictions, Credential state the person's credentials on that device, grouped as Problem , Waiting and Synchronized . For a problem the reason is shown for example Capacity exceeded or Invalid value . If nothing is listed, the person has no assigned access yet. What to do next A right is Assigned but not Applied : use Send access to the devices slug:person sync access and refresh. Rights come from policies. Granting and withdrawing them is described in Authorization slug:authorization . The devices are described in Devices slug:devices .

s: Use Synchronize Access to push the current access rights of one or more people to the devices.
x: Send access to the devices Access rights are normally passed to the devices automatically. If a right shows as not Applied on the Access state slug:person access tab, you can start a synchronization yourself. For one person 1. Open People . 2. On the person's card open the Commands menu key icon . 3. Choose Synchronize Access . For several people 1. Tick the people in the list. 2. Open the selected menu in the toolbar. 3. Choose Synchronize Access . The menu item shows its progress while it runs running, succeeded or failed . While devices are being synchronized, the progress is also shown in the side menu. When it finishes, the Access state tab of a person refreshes itself. If a credential does not reach a device, the Access state panel shows the reason; see Access of a person slug:person access .

s: See the history of events that concern one person, or watch them live.
x: Audit of a person Open the person and select the Audit tab. It shows the events that concern this person: changes to the person, credentials added or removed, and passages through doors where the person was recognised. It opens in History mode. History shows past events. Narrow them with Filters time range, event types, severity . Quick ranges such as Today , Last hour or Last week are offered. Live shows new events as they arrive. The same audit tool is used in other places; how to read and filter it is described in Audit slug:audit .

s: Permanently remove a person from the system.
x: Delete a person Deleting a person cannot be undone. From the list 1. Open People . 2. Click the Delete trash button on the person's card. 3. Read the list in the confirmation dialog and click Delete . From the person's page 1. Open the person and stay on the Settings tab. 2. Scroll to the Danger Zone , section Delete Person . 3. Click Delete and confirm. Once you delete a person, there is no going back. This action cannot be undone. If you only want to stop a person from getting in, it is safer to disable the person's credentials instead; see Change the status of a credential slug:credential manage .

s: Role profiles that hold adapter-specific person fields.
x: Profiles A profile is a role template. It holds values for the person fields that individual adapters access control systems need, so you define them once and reuse them. Open Profiles in the main menu. In this section: Create a profile slug:profile create Edit a profile slug:profile edit Delete a profile slug:profile delete Profile fields appear only for adapters that offer person profile fields; if none does, the page says No registered adapter exposes person profile fields.

s: Add a new role profile.
x: Create a profile 1. Open Profiles and click Add . 2. A profile named New Profile is created and its settings page opens. 3. Continue with Edit a profile slug:profile edit to name it and fill the fields. The list shows each profile with its name and chips for the adapters it covers. With none yet you see No profiles .

s: Rename a profile and fill adapter-specific fields.
x: Edit a profile Click a profile name or its pencil icon to open Profile Settings . 1. Change the Name required: Profile name is required. . 2. Under Adapters choose a tab per adapter and fill in its fields. 3. If a required field is empty you are asked to fill all required profile fields.

s: Remove one or several profiles.
x: Delete a profile One profile: click the bin icon on its card, or open its settings and use Delete in the Danger Zone Delete profile : removes the template and its adapter specific field values . Several: tick the checkboxes on the cards or Select All ; the toolbar shows how many are Selected with a menu of actions. Confirm the deletion; it cannot be undone.

s: Build automation rules that react to events or times, create incidents, send commands and notify people.
x: Scenarios A scenario is an automation rule. It waits for a trigger , such as an event, a time or a manual start, checks conditions , and then runs actions , for example create an incident, send a command to a device or notify a team. You build scenarios visually, by joining blocks in an editor, with no programming. Open Scenarios in the main menu. I want to... Go to See my scenarios and their state The scenario list slug:scenario list Make a new scenario Create a scenario slug:create scenario Load a scenario from a file Import a scenario slug:import scenario Save a scenario to a file Export a scenario slug:export scenario Copy a scenario Duplicate a scenario slug:duplicate scenario Turn a scenario on or off Enable or disable a scenario slug:enable disable scenario Remove a scenario Delete a scenario slug:delete scenario Learn the editor The scenario editor slug:scenario editor Choose when a scenario starts Triggers slug:scenario triggers Narrow which events match Conditions slug:scenario conditions Choose what happens Actions slug:scenario actions Give the operator a checklist Scenario instructions slug:scenario instructions Put event details into text Variables in text slug:scenario variables Try a scenario now Test run slug:scenario test run Follow a worked example Door forced open slug:scenario recipe door forced , Repeated access denials slug:scenario recipe repeated denials , Door held open at night slug:scenario recipe door held night , Connection lost slug:scenario recipe connection lost , Door not closed in time slug:scenario recipe door not closed , Morning check slug:scenario recipe morning check , Manual drill slug:scenario recipe manual drill Find out why a scenario does not work Troubleshooting slug:scenario troubleshooting See also the concept page Scenarios slug:concept scenarios . Incidents that scenarios create are handled in Incidents slug:incidents .

s: The Scenarios page: cards with state, owner and last change, and the actions on each card.
x: The scenario list Open Scenarios in the main menu. Each scenario is a card showing: its name and, if it has one, its description, a label Enabled or Disabled , with a green or grey icon, Last modified time, Owner , the person who created it "unknown" when not known . When there are none, the page says No Scenarios and invites you to create your first. Buttons on a card Icon Action Pencil Edit . Opens the editor slug:scenario editor . Clicking the name does the same. Pause or play Disable or Enable . See Enable or disable a scenario slug:enable disable scenario . Copy Duplicate . See Duplicate a scenario slug:duplicate scenario . Down arrow Export . See Export a scenario slug:export scenario . Bin Delete . See Delete a scenario slug:delete scenario . At the top Create Scenario , see Create a scenario slug:create scenario . Import , see Import a scenario slug:import scenario . A check box Select all . After you tick scenarios, the menu shows "N selected" and offers Delete . The search box in the top bar finds a scenario by name.

s: Name a new scenario and open the editor to build it. A new scenario starts disabled.
x: Create a scenario 1. Open Scenarios and click Create Scenario . 2. In Create New Scenario , type a Name . It is required: "Enter a descriptive name for this scenario". 3. Optionally type a Description . 4. Click Create . The scenario editor slug:scenario editor opens with an empty workspace. Build the rule and click Save . A new scenario is Disabled . It does nothing until you switch it on in the list. See Enable or disable a scenario slug:enable disable scenario . You can also start a scenario from an event in the audit. See Create a scenario from an event slug:audit create scenario . To start from a ready made file, see Import a scenario slug:import scenario .

s: Load a scenario that was exported from Protequ and open it in the editor, disabled.
x: Import a scenario 1. Open Scenarios and click Import . The Import Scenario window opens. 2. Click Choose file and pick a .json file that was made with Export slug:export scenario . The file may be at most 5 MB. 3. The scenario name is shown. The window reminds you: "The scenario is imported disabled. Fill in devices and other references in the editor." 4. Click Import . The scenario opens in the editor slug:scenario editor . Devices, people, spaces and teams are specific to an installation. After importing a scenario from another system, open each block that names one and pick the right item. Then save and enable slug:enable disable scenario the scenario. If the file is not a valid export, the window shows "The file is not a valid scenario export."

s: Download a scenario as a file to back it up or move it to another installation.
x: Export a scenario 1. Open Scenarios . 2. Click the down arrow icon, Export , on the scenario card. Your browser downloads the scenario as a file. Keep it as a backup, or load it into another installation with Import slug:import scenario . The file holds the rule itself. Devices and people it names belong to this installation and must be picked again after importing elsewhere.

s: Make a copy of a scenario to use as a starting point.
x: Duplicate a scenario 1. Open Scenarios . 2. Click the copy icon, Duplicate , on the scenario card. A copy is created and opened in the editor slug:scenario editor . Its name is the original name followed by " Copy ". The copy is Disabled , even if the original is enabled, so it cannot fire by accident. Change it, save it, and enable slug:enable disable scenario it when ready.

s: Switch a scenario on so it runs, or off so it is kept but ignored.
x: Enable or disable a scenario A scenario only runs while it is Enabled . A disabled scenario is kept with all its blocks but is ignored. 1. Open Scenarios . 2. On the scenario card, click the pause or play icon. It reads Enable on a disabled scenario and Disable on an enabled one. 3. The label on the card changes between Enabled and Disabled . New, duplicated and imported scenarios start Disabled . Always enable a scenario after you have built and tested it. See Test run slug:scenario test run .

s: Permanently remove one or several scenarios.
x: Delete a scenario Deleting is permanent. If you may need the scenario again, export it slug:export scenario first, or disable it slug:enable disable scenario instead. One scenario Click the bin icon, Delete , on the scenario card and confirm. Several scenarios 1. Tick the check boxes of the scenarios. 2. Open the menu that shows "N selected". 3. Choose Delete and confirm. The window lists the Items to delete and warns that the action cannot be undone.

s: The visual editor: the block toolbox, how to build a rule, and the Save, Test Run and Cancel buttons.
x: The scenario editor The editor opens when you create, import, duplicate or edit a scenario. The screen At the top left, the scenario Name . Click it to rename. At the top right, three buttons: Cancel , Test Run and Save . Below, the workspace where you build the rule, with the toolbox of blocks on the left. The toolbox has five groups: Group Contains Page Triggers When, Watch for, Every, At, Manual Triggers slug:scenario triggers Conditions Event, device and group state, filters, count and within, AND/OR/NOT Conditions slug:scenario conditions Actions Create incident, send command, send notification, send webhook Actions slug:scenario actions Instructions Steps the operator works through on the incident Scenario instructions slug:scenario instructions Variables Event details in text, and the association blocks Variables in text slug:scenario variables Build a rule 1. Drag one trigger block into the workspace. A scenario is one trigger with its conditions and actions. For two independent rules, make two scenarios. 2. Drag condition blocks into the trigger's conditions slot and snap them under each other. 3. Drag action blocks into the DO slot. 4. Fill in the fields of each block drop downs, text, pickers . 5. Click Save . Blocks only snap together where they fit, so the editor stops you from putting an action in a conditions slot. To delete a block, select it and press Delete. The buttons Save stores the rule. A green message "Scenario saved successfully" confirms it. If the rule is invalid, for example a block is incomplete, an error message tells what is wrong and nothing is saved. Test Run saves and then runs the scenario once. See Test run slug:scenario test run . Cancel returns to the list. Name and description are set when you create the scenario. Disabling and enabling is done in the list, see Enable or disable a scenario slug:enable disable scenario .

s: The five trigger blocks that decide when a scenario starts: When, Watch for, Every, At and Manual.
x: Triggers Every scenario starts with exactly one trigger block. Drag it from the Triggers group of the toolbox. Trigger Starts the scenario Fields WHEN when an event happens and the conditions inside it match a conditions slot and a DO slot for actions WATCH for when an expected event does not happen in time after another event an expected event slot, within a number of seconds, minutes or hours, an after slot for the starting event, and an ELSE slot for actions EVERY repeatedly at an interval a number and minutes or hours, then DO AT at fixed times of day on chosen days times as HH:MM separated by commas default 08:00 , the days Mo to Su Monday to Friday on by default , then DO MANUAL TRIGGER only when somebody starts it by hand DO only Which one to use React to something that happened: WHEN . React to something that did not happen, for example a door that was opened and not closed: WATCH for . Do something on a regular basis: EVERY or AT . A drill or a procedure that an operator starts: MANUAL TRIGGER . Scenarios with EVERY or AT have no triggering event. Their actions cannot use "source device", so pick a specific device or adapter. See worked examples: Door not closed in time slug:scenario recipe door not closed , Morning check slug:scenario recipe morning check , Manual drill slug:scenario recipe manual drill .

s: The blocks that narrow which events match: Event, filters, state checks, Count, Within and AND/OR/NOT.
x: Conditions Conditions go into the conditions slot of a trigger. Blocks placed one under another must all match. Event The Event block with a bell icon picks the kind of event. Click it and choose from the list, which holds every event the system knows, for example the entries that read "Door ... forced open", "Door ... held open" or "Access denied at ...". The first entry, Custom pattern... , lets you type an event pattern with a wildcard when no single event fits. Filters Filters narrow an event. Put them under the Event block. Block Narrows by from a device , person or space you pick. Tick with children to include the things inside it, for example the reader of a door or the doors of a room. severity a level with an operator: = , = or < than Info, Warning, Error, Alarm, Fire Alarm or Critical. between a time of day, from and to as HH:MM. An overnight range such as 22:00 to 06:00 works. on days of the week, Mo to Su. State checks Block Checks Device state that a chosen device IS or IS NOT in a chosen state, optionally held for at least a number of seconds, minutes or hours. Zero means the state right now. Group state that ALL , ANY or NONE of the devices in a chosen space ARE in a chosen state, optionally held for a time. Wrappers Block Meaning N+ times in matches when the event inside it happens N or more times in a window of seconds, minutes or hours. group by nothing, device or person counts each device or person separately. WITHIN matches when the events inside it happen in the given order within a time window. Logic AND all inside must match , OR any may match and NOT the inside must not match . Put condition blocks inside them to combine. Examples: Repeated access denials slug:scenario recipe repeated denials , Door held open at night slug:scenario recipe door held night .

s: The blocks that say what happens: create an incident, send a command, send a notification or call a web address.
x: Actions Actions go into the DO slot of a trigger the ELSE slot of WATCH for . They run one after another. Create incident Opens an incident slug:incidents for operators. Severity : Warning, Info, Error, Alarm, Fire Alarm or Critical. Title : the text operators see. It can contain variables slug:scenario variables , and starts as $match.scenarioName . Associations : blocks you plug in to attach context to the incident, such as a device, a person, a note or a key and value. See Variables in text slug:scenario variables . Instructions : the steps for the operator. See Scenario instructions slug:scenario instructions . Send command Sends a command to a device or an adapter. Choose the target: source device the device that produced the event , specific device , or adapter . Choose the command . The list offers the commands the target supports. If a device has none, the list says "No commands available for this device". For some video commands you can add a person with for . Source device is not offered in scenarios that start with EVERY or AT , because they have no event. Send notification to : the team to notify. via : Email , SMS or Push . message : the text. Send webhook Calls an address on the web. Choose the method POST, GET, PUT, DELETE , the URL , optional Headers and Body , and the Content Type application/json, application/x www form urlencoded or text/plain . Examples: Door forced open slug:scenario recipe door forced , Connection lost slug:scenario recipe connection lost .

s: Add a checklist of steps to the incidents a scenario creates, so operators know what to do.
x: Scenario instructions When a scenario creates an incident, you can attach a checklist that the operator works through. The steps appear in the incident as Instructions . See Incident instructions slug:incident instructions . 1. Add a Create incident action to the scenario. 2. Find its Instructions slot. 3. From the Instructions group of the toolbox, drag step blocks into that slot, one under another. Step blocks Block The operator gets Info a text to read. Mandatory ones must be confirmed. Note prompt a box to type a note into. Command a button that runs a command on a device. Command on space a button that runs a command on a space. Show on map a button that jumps to a place. Verify person a button to look at a person. Capture snapshot a button that takes a snapshot. Escalate a button that escalates to a chosen person. Notify a button that sends a notification channel, recipient, message . Most steps have a text label and a Mandatory check box. A mandatory step must be done before the incident can be resolved. See Resolve an incident slug:incident resolve . Command, Show on map, Verify person and Capture snapshot can point at Source of alarm , the device or place that raised the incident, or at a Chosen target that you pick.

s: Insert details of the event or the scenario into titles, notes and messages.
x: Variables in text In text fields, such as an incident title or a note, you can write a variable . It is replaced by the real value when the scenario runs. Variable Replaced by $match.scenarioName name of the scenario $event.device the device that produced the event $event.person the person in the event $event.type the kind of event $event.severity the severity of the event $event.timestamp the time of the event Example title: Forced door at $event.device You can type a variable, or drag the Variables blocks. The Variables group of the toolbox also has a block that picks a variable from a list and a plain text block. Association blocks The group Associations holds blocks that you plug into a Create incident action to attach context: Block Attaches device a chosen device person a chosen person note a text, which may contain variables starts as $match.scenarioName key = value a detail, with a variable as the value Which variables are offered depends on the trigger. An event trigger offers the event ones. A scheduled trigger offers none about an event, because nothing triggered it.

s: Save a scenario and run it once from the editor to see that it works.
x: Test run 1. Open the scenario in the editor slug:scenario editor . 2. Click Test Run . The scenario is saved first. If the rule is invalid, the error is shown and nothing runs. Then the application asks the system to run it. The message "Scenario started successfully." confirms the start. A scenario with a MANUAL TRIGGER is the natural thing to test this way, because nothing else starts it. If it fails Message Meaning "You do not have permission to run this scenario." Your account may not run it. "Scenario is missing or its definition could not be compiled." The scenario is missing, disabled or cannot be run by hand. "Scenario run failed." Any other failure. Try again, or ask your administrator. Test with care. Actions are real: a test run creates a real incident, sends real commands and sends real notifications. Related pages: Enable or disable a scenario slug:enable disable scenario , Troubleshooting slug:scenario troubleshooting .

s: Example: create an alarm incident and email the security team when a door is forced open.
x: Example: door forced open Goal. When somebody forces a door open, create an Alarm incident and notify the security team. Rule. text WHEN Event: Door ... forced open from device: Main Entrance Door, with children DO Create incident Severity: Alarm Title: Forced door at $event.device Send notification to: Security Team via: Email message: Forced door event detected Steps. 1. Create a scenario slug:create scenario and drag WHEN into the workspace. 2. Drag an Event block into its conditions slot. Click it and pick the entry "Door ... forced open". 3. Drag a from block under the Event. Choose device , pick the door, and tick with children so the reader on the door counts too. 4. Drag Create incident into DO . Set Severity to Alarm and the Title to Forced door at $event.device . 5. Drag Send notification under it. Pick the team, choose Email and type the message. 6. Click Save , then enable the scenario slug:enable disable scenario in the list. Result. When the door or a device under it reports a forced open event, an Alarm incident is created and the team is emailed. Related pages: Triggers slug:scenario triggers , Conditions slug:scenario conditions , Actions slug:scenario actions .

s: Example: react only when the same person is refused three times in five minutes.
x: Example: repeated access denials Goal. Notify security only when a failed access pattern shows up, not for a single refusal. Rule. text WHEN 3+ times in 5 minutes group by: person Event: Access denied at ... from space: Server Room, with children DO Create incident Severity: Warning Title: Repeated access denied for $event.person Send notification to: Security Team via: Push message: Repeated access denied near Server Room Steps. 1. Create a scenario slug:create scenario and drag WHEN into the workspace. 2. Drag the N+ times in block into its conditions slot. Set 3 , 5 and minutes , and group by to person so each person is counted separately. 3. Drag an Event block inside it and pick the entry "Access denied at ...". 4. Drag a from block under the counter block. Choose space , pick the room, tick with children . 5. Add Create incident Warning, title Repeated access denied for $event.person and Send notification under DO . 6. Save and enable slug:enable disable scenario . Result. Nothing happens for the first two refusals. The third within five minutes by the same person creates one incident and one notification. Related pages: Conditions slug:scenario conditions .

s: Example: ignore doors held open by day but raise an incident at night.
x: Example: door held open at night Goal. Ignore normal daytime held open events, but escalate them at night. Rule. text WHEN AND Event: Door ... held open from space: Warehouse, with children between 22:00 and 06:00 DO Create incident Severity: Alarm Title: Door held open during night Steps. 1. Create a scenario slug:create scenario and drag WHEN into the workspace. 2. Drag AND into its conditions slot. 3. Inside AND , drag an Event block "Door ... held open" , a from block space, the warehouse, with children and a between block 22:00 and 06:00 . 4. Drag Create incident into DO , Severity Alarm, Title Door held open during night . 5. Optionally add Send command with source device as the target to act on the door that raised the event. 6. Save and enable slug:enable disable scenario . Result. A held open event during the day is ignored. At night it creates an incident. Related pages: Conditions slug:scenario conditions , Actions slug:scenario actions .

s: Example: tell the maintenance team when a device in a building loses its connection.
x: Example: connection lost Goal. Notify maintenance when a device in a chosen building loses its connection. Rule. text WHEN Event: Connection lost to ... from space: Building A, with children DO Create incident Severity: Error Title: Connection lost: $event.device Send notification to: Maintenance Team via: Email message: Connection lost in Building A Steps. 1. Create a scenario slug:create scenario and drag WHEN into the workspace. 2. Drag an Event block into the conditions slot and pick the entry "Connection lost to ...". 3. Under it drag a from block: space , Building A, with children. 4. Under DO add Create incident Error, title Connection lost: $event.device and Send notification the maintenance team, Email . 5. Save and enable slug:enable disable scenario . Result. Every connection lost event in the building creates an Error incident and emails maintenance.

s: Example: raise an incident when a held-open door is not closed within five minutes.
x: Example: door not closed in time Goal. Create an incident when a door held open event is not followed by a door closed event within five minutes. Rule. text WATCH for Event: Door ... closed within 5 minutes after Event: Door ... held open ELSE Create incident Severity: Alarm Title: Door was not closed in time Steps. 1. Create a scenario slug:create scenario and drag WATCH for into the workspace. 2. Drag an Event block into the expected event slot and pick "Door ... closed". 3. Set within to 5 and minutes . 4. Drag an Event block into the after slot and pick "Door ... held open". 5. Drag Create incident into the ELSE slot: Severity Alarm, Title Door was not closed in time . 6. Save and enable slug:enable disable scenario . Result. After a held open event the system waits for the close event. If it does not come within five minutes, the incident is created. Related pages: Triggers slug:scenario triggers .

s: Example: notify operators every weekday at 08:00.
x: Example: morning check Goal. Remind operators every weekday morning to do a daily check. Rule. text AT 08:00 on Mo Tu We Th Fr DO Send notification to: Operators via: Push message: Morning access control check started Steps. 1. Create a scenario slug:create scenario and drag AT into the workspace. 2. Leave the time at 08:00 . Several times can be typed separated by commas, for example 08:00, 14:00 . 3. Make sure Mo to Fr are ticked and Sa and Su are not. This is the default. 4. Drag Send notification into DO . Pick the team, choose Push and type the message. 5. Save and enable slug:enable disable scenario . Result. The notification goes out at 08:00 on weekdays. Related pages: Triggers slug:scenario triggers .

s: Example: a scenario that runs only when an operator starts it, for a planned drill.
x: Example: manual drill Goal. An operator started scenario for a planned drill. Rule. text MANUAL TRIGGER DO Create incident Severity: Warning Title: Manual lockdown drill Send command target: specific device command: a lock command the device supports Steps. 1. Create a scenario slug:create scenario and drag MANUAL TRIGGER into the workspace. 2. Drag Create incident into DO : Severity Warning, Title Manual lockdown drill . 3. Drag Send command under it. A manual scenario has no source event, so choose specific device as the target, pick the device and pick a command it supports. 4. Save and enable slug:enable disable scenario . 5. Start it with Test run slug:scenario test run when the drill begins. Result. The scenario runs only when started by hand.

s: What to check when a scenario never runs, runs too often or does nothing.
x: Troubleshooting scenarios Problem Check The scenario never runs Is it Enabled in the list? New, duplicated and imported scenarios start Disabled . See Enable or disable a scenario slug:enable disable scenario . Does it have exactly one trigger block? Save shows an error The rule is incomplete or invalid. Read the message, fix the block it names and save again. It runs too often Add a from , severity or between filter. Use N+ times in to react only to repeats. It runs for the wrong door Check the from block. Without with children the events of a door's reader are not included. A scheduled scenario cannot use the source device EVERY and AT have no triggering event. Pick a specific device or adapter. An incident title shows a variable name instead of a value The variable is not available for that trigger. See Variables in text slug:scenario variables . Send command does nothing Is a command picked, and does the target support it? Test Run says the scenario is missing See Test run slug:scenario test run . An imported scenario does nothing It imports disabled and its devices need to be picked again. See Import a scenario slug:import scenario . To see what actually happened, look at the incidents the scenario created Incidents slug:incidents and at the audit slug:audit .

s: Organise your site into spaces, assign devices to them and see who is inside.
x: Spaces A space is a place in your site: a building, a floor, a lab, a car park. Spaces form a hierarchy, so a building can contain floors and a floor can contain rooms. Devices such as readers and doors are assigned to spaces, and access rights can refer to a space. Open Spaces in the main menu. Opening a space gives you these tabs: Space Settings , Spaces its sub spaces , Devices , Audit and Space occupancy . I want to... Go to See and browse all spaces Space list slug:space list Create a space Create a space slug:create space Rename, move, set antipassback or occupancy limits, delete Space settings slug:space settings Assign devices to a space or remove them Space devices slug:space devices See who is inside right now Space occupancy slug:space occupancy See events for a space Space audit slug:space audit Related: Devices slug:devices , People slug:people .

s: Browse the space hierarchy, jump into sub-spaces and delete spaces.
x: Space list Choose Spaces in the main menu. The page shows the top level spaces as cards. On the Spaces tab of a space you see the sub spaces of that space in the same way. What a card shows The space picture, name and description. Under Spaces , a chip for each sub space. Click a chip to open that sub space. The icon buttons on a card are: Pencil : open the space settings, see Space settings slug:space settings . Plus : add a sub space inside this space, see Create a space slug:create space . Device icon : open the devices of the space, see Space devices slug:space devices . Bin : delete the space. Clicking the name or picture also opens the settings. If no space exists yet the page says "No Spaces Found" and suggests Add Space . Select and delete several spaces 1. Tick the checkbox on each card, or tick Select All . 2. Open the "N selected" menu and choose the delete command. 3. Confirm in the dialog. Deleting cannot be undone. Compact view Turn on Compact view to show one line per space. With a very long list it is switched on and locked.

s: Add a new top-level space or a sub-space.
x: Create a space 1. Open Spaces and click Add Space . To create a sub space directly, click the plus icon on the parent space's card instead; the parent is then pre selected. 2. In the dialog Create New Space , fill in: Space Name : required, and it should be unique. Description : a short text, optional. Parent Space : choose the space this one sits in, or No Parent Top Level . 3. Click Create Space . Cancel closes the dialog without creating. After creation the settings of the new space open, see Space settings slug:space settings . Next you usually assign devices slug:space devices .

s: Rename or move a space, set antipassback and occupancy thresholds, change its picture or delete it.
x: Space settings Open a space and choose the Space Settings tab. General Space Name : required, and it should be unique. Description : a short text. Parent Space : change it to move the space. No Parent Top Level makes it a top level space. The space itself and its own sub spaces cannot be chosen. Space Image : click Upload Image to replace the picture JPG, PNG or SVG . Antipassback Antipassback stops a credential being used to enter twice without leaving in between, or to let a second person in on the same card. APB Mode : Off , Soft allow + warning or Hard deny on violation . Timed Reset seconds : clears the antipassback state automatically after this time. 0 means never. Global APB mode : Off or Soft . Watches movement between spaces and warns about violations. Antipassback needs to know the direction of each reader. Set it in Space devices slug:space devices with Reader Role Entry or Exit . Occupancy thresholds Occupancy counts the people currently inside the space see Space occupancy slug:space occupancy . You can have Protequ raise an event when the count crosses a limit: Upper threshold : an event is raised when occupancy reaches or exceeds this value minimum 1 . Lower threshold : an event is raised when occupancy drops to or below this value minimum 0 . Clear a field to switch that limit off. Delete a space In the red Danger Zone click Delete Space and confirm. Deleting cannot be undone. After deleting you return to the space list.

s: Assign existing devices to a space, set reader direction and remove devices from it.
x: Space devices Open a space and choose the Devices tab. It lists the devices assigned to the space. Add devices 1. Click Add Existing Device . 2. In the dialog select one or more devices. Devices already in the space are not offered. 3. Confirm. The devices appear in the list. You cannot create a new device here. Use Add a device slug:add device first. What a device card shows The device name, state and picture, and its Commands menu the same commands as in the device list slug:device list . If the space uses antipassback or occupancy limits, the card also shows Reader Role : Entry : a successful passage adds the person to the space. Exit : a successful passage removes the person from the space. The same reader can be Entry in one space and Exit in another. Without antipassback or occupancy thresholds on the space the role is hidden, see Space settings slug:space settings . Remove a device from the space Click the bin icon on the card, or select several cards and choose the remove command from the "N selected" menu. This only removes the assignment; the device itself is not deleted.

s: See how many people are in a space right now and correct the list by hand.
x: Space occupancy Open a space and choose the Space occupancy tab. What you see Current occupancy : the number of different people inside the space. A table with Person click the name to open the person and Last entered date and time in your local time zone . People whose name is not known are shown as Unknown person . The page updates by itself while it is open. How people get on the list Occupancy is passive and never blocks anyone. A successful passage at a reader with the role Entry adds the person, and at a reader with the role Exit removes the person. For this to work the readers of the space need a role, see Space devices slug:space devices . Correct the list If someone left without using an exit reader, click the person remove icon at the end of the row Remove person from occupancy . The person is dropped from the count. Warning message "Occupancy projection is recovering. Data may be temporarily unavailable." appears for a short time after a restart. Wait and the figures return. Limits Set upper and lower thresholds in Space settings slug:space settings to be notified when the count gets too high or low.

s: Browse the event history of one space.
x: Space audit Open a space and choose the Audit tab. It shows the events recorded for that space, such as the space being created, moved or changed, and devices being added to it or removed. It opens in history mode. You can filter and search the list in the same way as in the main audit view. See Audit slug:audit .

s: What teams are, how they are organised and where to manage them.
x: Teams A team is a named group of people. Teams exist so that you give access once to the group instead of to each person: everyone in the team gets the rights of the team. Teams can contain sub teams , so you can mirror your organisation for example a company, its departments, and their shifts . Open Teams in the main menu. The list shows the top level teams; open a team to see its sub teams. A team has these tabs: Tab What it is for Team Settings Name, description, parent team, image, delete. See Edit a team slug:team edit . Sub teams Teams directly below this team. See Sub teams slug:team subteams . Team Members The people in the team. See Team members slug:team members . Audit History of the team. See Audit of a team slug:team audit . Common tasks Create a team slug:team create Edit a team slug:team edit Work with sub teams slug:team subteams Add or remove team members slug:team members Delete a team slug:team delete Access of a team Teams have no separate access page. Access rights are given to a team as policies, see Authorization slug:authorization . Each member then sees the result on the Access state tab of the person, where the policy is labelled with the team it came from; see Access of a person slug:person access .

s: Add a new team, optionally below another team.
x: Create a team 1. Open Teams in the main menu. 2. Click Add New Team top right . To create a team directly below an existing team, click the Add New Team + button on that team's card instead. 3. In Create New Team fill in: Field Notes Team Name Required. Use a unique name. Description Optional short description. Parent Team Pick the team above, or No Parent Top Level . 4. Click Create Team . The new team opens on its Team Settings tab. Click Cancel to close without creating. Next: Add people to the team slug:team members .

s: Change the name, description, parent team and image of a team.
x: Edit a team Open Teams , click the team, and stay on the Team Settings tab. Field Notes Team Name Required; cannot be left empty. Description Short description, shown on the team's card. Parent Team Moves the team below another team, or to No Parent Top Level . Teams below this team are listed as Team is already a children and cannot be chosen, so a team can never end up inside itself. There is no Save button. Team image Click Upload Image . Supported formats: JPG, PNG, SVG. Maximum size: 5 MB. Delete See Delete a team slug:team delete .

s: Build a hierarchy of teams and navigate it.
x: Sub teams Teams form a tree. The Teams page in the main menu lists teams without a parent. Open a team and select the Sub teams tab to see the teams directly below it. Teams on a card are also shown as chips under Sub teams . To add a sub team, click the Add New Team + button on the parent team's card, or use Add New Team while on the Sub teams tab. The parent is preset; see Create a team slug:team create . To move a team elsewhere, change Parent Team in its settings; see Edit a team slug:team edit . Each card has the buttons Edit Team settings , Add New Team , Edit Members and Delete . Members of a sub team are not listed in the parent team's Team Members tab.

s: Add new or existing people to a team and remove them from it.
x: Team members Open the team and select the Team Members tab. It lists the people directly in the team, shown like the People list slug:people find . Add a person who does not exist yet 1. Click Add New Person . 2. Fill in the dialog see Create a person slug:person create and confirm. The person is created and is already in this team. Add existing people 1. Click Add Existing Person . 2. Search for people, pick one or more they appear as chips , and confirm. Only people who are not yet in the team are offered. Remove people from the team Removing someone from a team does not delete the person. One person: click the Delete trash button on the person's card. Its action is remove from this team . Several: tick the people, open the selected menu and choose Remove . Confirm the dialog. If the team is empty you see No People Found .

s: History of changes and events that concern one team.
x: Audit of a team Open the team and select the Audit tab. It opens in History mode and shows events about this team, for example that it was created, renamed, moved, or that a person was added or removed. Switch to Live to watch events as they arrive. Narrow the list with Filters . How to read and filter audit lists is described in Audit slug:audit .

s: Permanently remove a team.
x: Delete a team Deleting a team cannot be undone. The people in the team are not deleted. From the list Click the Delete trash button on the team's card and confirm in the dialog. From the team's page 1. Open the team, Team Settings tab. 2. In the Danger Zone , section Delete Team , click Delete . 3. Confirm. You return to the Teams list. Once you delete a team, there is no going back. This action cannot be undone. To only take one person out of a team see Team members slug:team members .
